findings.user_impact: The visitor leaves unsure what was recorded or what happens next. Her last spoken words are a brand tagline instead of their spot.
findings.recommendation: Make WRAP a one-line recap: name, business and the email read back, then 'Anything you want to ask before I lock it in?'. CLOSE, after the save returns: 'You're in, {name} — number {position} on the list. Your invite comes to that email when early access opens.' Speak the position only when the sheet returned it (UX-02). Keep 'a product by Omnikom' on screen only. In Retell, save_lead returns the position (retell-migration.md step 5), and end_call fires after this line.

findings.title: The prompt contradicts itself: reveal vs drive rule, followUp null, word cap, and worked examples that can't happen at runtime
findings.evidence: REVEAL says 'Do not ask for anything in this turn' (mary-prompt.server.ts:121). The drive rule says 'every turn must END on one concrete move' (:160). The prompt says 'followUp… is null only on a closing, exit or final callback turn' (:164), while the playbook says 'Or null when a reaction alone is right' (mary-voice.md:422-424). The word cap is 'roughly 25 words for the whole turn' (mary-voice.md:426), yet live replies ran 31 (call 2) and 33 words (call 4). The worked examples show MARY taking two turns in a row (mary-voice.md:455-459, 543-546), which the runner can't do. The phase is computed from the fields known before this turn (mary-prompt.server.ts:100-102), so the turn that completes discovery is told 'draw out what is still missing'. In live call 4 the model revealed anyway, against its instruction.
findings.user_impact: On each turn the model has to guess which rule wins, so behaviour varies from call to call: a reveal with or without a question, long turns in a loud room, discovery questions after everything is known.
findings.recommendation: Add REVEAL as an explicit exception to the drive rule. Make the cap hard (25 words or fewer, LANES 35 or fewer) and check it in finishTurn. Rewrite the examples so every MARY turn follows a Person line. Add: 'If their last message supplies the last missing detail, act on the next phase now.' In Retell, split the phases into multi-prompt states with explicit transitions (https://docs.retellai.com/build/single-multi-prompt/write-multi-prompt).

findings.title: Porting the playbook to Retell as it is would raise the per-minute cost and keep lines that tell people to hold a button
findings.evidence: The system prompt is the whole playbook: 28,135 characters, about 7,000 tokens (docs/mary-voice.md via mary-prompt.server.ts:4,9), plus about 1k tokens of per-turn rules. Retell bills duration × (prompt tokens ÷ 4,000) above 4,000 tokens, and the count includes the transcript (https://docs.retellai.com/accounts/billing-exceptions). So every call starts at 1.75× billed duration or more and grows. Hold-button lines are at mary-voice.md:3-4 and :343-344 ('ask them to hold the button'). The migration plan pulls post-call analysis fields industry and business (docs/architecture/retell-migration.md:97-99), which are ungrounded LLM extractions.
findings.user_impact: Running costs go up, MARY tells people to press a button that no longer exists, and invented industries come back into the sheet from call analysis.
findings.recommendation: Port it as a multi-prompt agent with a global prompt under 4,000 tokens. Move objection lines into per-state prompts and drop the worked examples from the always-on context. Rewrite the hold-button lines. Name tools explicitly in the prompt, per Retell's guide: 'call save_lead as soon as name and email are confirmed…; call end_call after the close/exit/final callback line'. Use call_analyzed only for summary and outcome, and never let it overwrite grounded fields. Before launch, run Retell LLM simulation cases for every scenario in this list (https://docs.retellai.com/test/llm-simulation-testing; UX-60).

findings.title: The landing page doesn't prepare visitors for the mic prompt, what MARY will ask, or how long the call really takes
findings.evidence: The landing text (scratchpad/ux-audit/funnel/log-landing-ios.json) is 'Meet MARY. Your AI Revenue Concierge. Talk to her for two minutes…'. There is no mic pre-prompt: start() goes straight to getUserMedia (mary-app.tsx:517), and landing.tsx:139-165 never mentions the mic. The preview bubble 'Hi, I'm MARY. Want first access…' (landing.tsx:9) is not what she says (UX-08). On the 'two minutes' claim: the funnel lens timed the docs/mary-voice.md §10 worked example (10 MARY turns, 19 beats, 243 words) at the measured 0.42 s/word, 2.98 s turn latency, 1.28 s TTS start and 1.8 s follow-up gaps, which comes to about 3.1 min even for a terse caller (worked-example.txt). The market lens estimated the happy path at about 2.2-2.6 min. What OmniSuite does appears only in the 0.7rem footer. web.dev permissions guidance: 'preface the permission prompt with why the prompt is needed' (web.dev/articles/permissions-best-practices, 2024).
findings.user_impact: The native mic sheet appears without warning, the expectations ('2 min', 'first access') don't match the call, and the headline sells the agent rather than the visitor's benefit. All of this lowers Start and mic-allow rates.
findings.recommendation: Under the CTA, add: 'She'll ask for your microphone. About 3 minutes. She'll ask your name, business and email.' Replace the preview bubble with her real opener. Add a one-line benefit ('Early access + launch pricing for teams that live on leads'). With Retell the mic stays open for the whole call, so the priming copy must say so. Lower latency shortens the call only slightly, because about 100 s of it is her speech.

findings.title: The 'your turn' cue is an 11 px grey line, and the big button looks the same whether MARY is talking or waiting
findings.evidence: The hold button reads 'Hold to talk to MARY' both while she speaks and while she waits (composer.tsx:94-98). log-voice-desktop.json shows hold='Hold to talk to MARY' with the status 'MARY is speaking · hold to cut in', then 'Hold the button or the space bar…'. Only the status line changes, and it is text-[0.7rem] and muted (composer.tsx:303). Compare scratchpad/ux-audit/funnel/shots/voice-desktop-08-mid-welcome.png with voice-desktop-10-your-turn.png. During the 1.8 s gap between her two beats, the status still says 'MARY is speaking' while she is silent (voice-ios-09-between-beats.png).
findings.user_impact: First-time voice users don't know when to answer. Some talk over her and cut her off (UX-09); others wait in silence.
findings.recommendation: Show distinct floor states on the primary control: 'MARY is talking…' (muted, subtle waveform), then 'Your turn: hold to answer' (full colour, one pulse, optional haptic via navigator.vibrate on Android). Raise the status text to at least 14px. This conflicts with UX-77, which would keep the button label constant and let the orb carry state; choose one approach. With Retell, drive the same states from the SDK's agent start/stop-talking and transcript events. The hold button goes away, but the listening and your-turn states still have to be designed.

findings.title: Hold-to-talk is the default, while the market standard is an open mic you can interrupt
findings.evidence: The initial talkMode is 'hold' (src/features/mary/conversation/reducer.ts:17). The hold button is a full-width 64px bar (composer.tsx:83) that dominates the phone screen (scratchpad/ux-audit/funnel/shots/convo-ios-15-progress-pills.png). The ElevenLabs, Vapi and Sesame demos all run an open mic (captures under scratchpad/browser and scratchpad/ux-audit/market/shots). GPT-Live-1 (GA 2026-09-10) is full-duplex with 'almost 80% fewer interruptions' (https://www.testingcatalog.com/openai-launches-gpt-live-1-for-full-duplex-voice-agents/). Retell exposes interruption_sensitivity, responsiveness, enable_dynamic_responsiveness and denoising_mode 'noise-and-background-speech-cancellation' (https://docs.retellai.com/api-references/create-agent), the last at +$0.005/min (https://www.retellai.com/pricing).
findings.user_impact: Hold-to-talk feels like a walkie-talkie rather than a phone call. Visitors have to learn a gesture, keep a finger on the screen and remember to let go, and a missed hold brings 'Didn't catch that' notices. That weakens the landing page's 'talk to her like a person' promise.
findings.recommendation: Under Retell, default to an open mic, with denoising_mode noise-and-background-speech-cancellation and interruption_sensitivity tuned below 1 for speakerphone use. Replace the hold bar with a visible mute toggle (ElevenLabs turned muting on by default on 2026-08-24) and keep 'Type instead'. Keep hold-to-talk only as a manual 'noisy room' option if testing shows it is still needed.

findings.title: A fixed boot screen and staggered entrance animations hold back the Start button by about 1.7 s after first paint on every visit
findings.evidence: MIN_BOOT_MS 900 + BOOT_FADE_MS 500 (mary-app.tsx:78-79), plus CTA entrance delays of up to 0.4-0.45 s + 0.7 s (landing.tsx:77-81,142-145). The whole app is ClientOnly, so the server HTML contains only the boot screen (src/routes/index.tsx:37-42; funnel live.html has no body copy). Measured across 5 live runs by the visual lens: FCP 1536/1600/1784/2000/1948 ms and CTA usable at 3284/3336/3523/3720/3698 ms, a constant gap of 1720-1750 ms (scratchpad/ux-audit/visual/log-*.txt 'cta'). Funnel lens: Start is in the DOM 2.6 s after navigation on a fast connection (log-landing-ios.json), and 3.0-3.2 s on throttled slow 4G with 348 KB transferred (slow-net.mjs). JS: 107.5 KB + 94.6 KB + 11.4 KB compressed.
findings.user_impact: Every visitor, including returning ones and ad clicks, waits almost 2 s of pure animation before they can press Start. On congested conference Wi-Fi they stare at 'Preparing your conversation' before the value proposition appears. It feels slow rather than premium.
findings.recommendation: Server-render the static landing (headline and CTA paint with the HTML) and keep only the call engine client-side, which removes the boot gate. If the gate stays, show it only when hydration takes more than 300 ms and set MIN_BOOT_MS to 0. Bring the CTA in first, at 250 ms or less, and the decorative preview after it.

findings.title: Share previews and the canonical URL point to omnisuite.omnikom.ai, a domain that does not exist (NXDOMAIN)
findings.evidence: src/routes/index.tsx:8 sets SITE_URL = 'https://omnisuite.omnikom.ai'. The live HTML serves og:image https://omnisuite.omnikom.ai/og-omnisuite.jpg, plus og:url, twitter:image and rel=canonical, all on .ai (scratchpad/ux-audit/funnel/live.html, visual/live/index.html). https://dns.google/resolve?name=omnisuite.omnikom.ai returns Status 3 (NXDOMAIN), and so does omnikom.ai. omnisuite.omnikom.io resolves to 185.158.133.1, and https://omnisuite.omnikom.io/og-omnisuite.jpg returns 200 (58,131 bytes).
findings.user_impact: Every link shared on iMessage, WhatsApp, LinkedIn or Slack (the conference and referral channels) shows no preview image, and search engines are told the page lives on a dead domain. This is the first impression for most referred visitors.
findings.recommendation: Set SITE_URL to https://omnisuite.omnikom.io, or read it from an env var or the request host. Re-check with a link-preview debugger after deploy.

findings.title: The live typing box is 14 px on phones, so iPhone Safari zooms the whole call screen when it is tapped
findings.evidence: scratchpad/ux-audit/visual/textarea.mjs on live, 390x844, iPhone user agent: the computed textarea font-size is 14px, with class 'max-h-24 … text-sm'. The viewport meta has no maximum-scale (src/routes/__root.tsx:84). The repo has the correct 16 px (composer.tsx:284 'text-base … sm:text-sm'), so this is a live-only regression, part of UX-14. Safari zooms focused inputs rendered below 16 px and does not zoom back out (https://defensivecss.dev/tip/input-zoom-safari/, https://css-tricks.com/16px-or-larger-text-prevents-ios-form-zoom/).
findings.user_impact: People who choose 'Type instead' (loud rooms, mic denied) see the page zoom in on focus. The header, orb and hold button slide off-screen and the page stays zoomed after sending, which feels broken on the fallback path.
findings.recommendation: When the live code is reconciled (UX-14), restore text-base (16 px) on the textarea below sm, as in the repo. Check any other input, including the owner vault's.

findings.title: Emails and phone numbers typed on a phone get iOS auto-capitalisation and autocorrect, and no email or number keypad
findings.evidence: The composer textarea (composer.tsx:258-285) has no inputMode, autoCapitalize, autoCorrect, spellCheck or autoComplete. The turn already returns nextField (mary.functions.ts:53), but nothing under src/features/mary keeps it. Safari iOS support (MDN browser-compat-data 8.1.3, 2026-09-24): autocapitalize 10.3+, autocorrect 14.5+, inputmode 12.2+.
findings.user_impact: 'Sarah@brightpath.com' starts with a capital letter, domain words can be 'corrected', and there is no number keypad for the phone number. The typos land in exactly the two fields that make the lead reachable.
findings.recommendation: Keep turn.nextField in the session reducer. In composer.tsx, when nextField is 'email', set inputMode='email', autoCapitalize='none', autoCorrect='off', spellCheck={false} and autoComplete='email'. When it is 'phone', set inputMode='tel' and autoComplete='tel'. Consider an <input> for those two turns so iOS AutoFill can offer the visitor's own email and number.

findings.title: The end screen offers no next action: no share link, and no booking slot for callbacks
findings.evidence: The signed-up end screen ends with 'Start another conversation' (end-screen.tsx:176-183), and the funnel lens's end-button list has no share or referral link (log-convo-desktop.json). The callback copy promises 'A real person calls you on …' with no time (conversation/text.ts:65-75). Best practice: 'give them something to do - a referral link' at 'the highest-intent moment you will get from that person for weeks' (https://21st.dev/blog/react-waitlist-page-components, 2026-08-20). LaunchList (2026) also says referral and share prompts work best right at sign-up. Retell's homepage demo is itself 'Lead Qualification' leading to a scheduled call (scratchpad/ux-audit/market/sites-ios.json), and Retell is moving booking to its Cal.com integration by 10/31/2026 (https://docs.retellai.com/deprecation-notice/overview).
findings.user_impact: Qualified, excited visitors leave with nothing to do. Callback requests become 'someone will call at some point', and hot leads cool off while they wait.
findings.recommendation: On the signed-up screen, add one share action (the Web Share API native sheet with the site URL; add referral tracking later) and keep 'Start another conversation' secondary. Put the same share link in the confirmation email (UX-10). On the callback screen, add a 'Pick a time' Cal.com booking link prefilled with name and email. With Retell, MARY can offer times during the call through the Cal.com integration instead of promising a callback.

findings.title: No 'all lines busy' state: Retell allows 20 concurrent calls by default, and a launch spike will exceed that
findings.evidence: 'Pay-As-You-Go workspaces are allocated a quota of 20 concurrent calls by default … All active voice calls draw from the same concurrency pool.' Burst is capped at 3× and adds $0.10/min for the whole call (https://docs.retellai.com/deploy/concurrency). ElevenLabs' widget added 'concurrency queue status' on 2026-08-24 (https://elevenlabs.io/docs/changelog/2026/8/24). MARY's start() (mary-app.tsx:508-536) has no busy or capacity branch.
findings.user_impact: On launch day (Product Hunt, a newsletter), visitor 21 and up would get a failed call at exactly the moment demand peaks, and those leads are most likely lost.
findings.recommendation: When web-call creation fails with a concurrency error, show a warm 'MARY is on a lot of calls right now' state. Offer to switch to typing (which still uses /api/turn) and, once built, 'Call me instead' (UX-61), keeping the collected fields. Turn on burst for launch days, and budget extra concurrency from the expected peak.

findings.title: MARY goes silent while save_lead runs; Retell's speak-during-execution and filler speech can cover it
findings.evidence: Today the end screen shows 'Securing your place…' while the sheet call runs (end-screen.tsx:81), and during a call only '…' appears while she is thinking (call-stage.tsx:255). Retell custom functions support 'Speak During Execution', e.g. 'Let me retrieve that information for you' (https://docs.retellai.com/build/single-multi-prompt/custom-function). By default a function 'isn't retried — if the request fails or times out, the agent receives the error message' (https://docs.retellai.com/build/conversation-flow/custom-function). ElevenLabs recommends 3.0 s soft-timeout fillers (https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/customization/conversation-flow), and GPT-Live-1 'can keep a conversation moving while … actions run' (2026-09-10).
findings.user_impact: The Apps Script write plus the position lookup can take seconds. Without a filler, MARY goes quiet at the very moment the visitor is being signed up, which sounds like a dropped call.
findings.recommendation: Turn on speak_during_execution for save_lead with a line in MARY's voice ('One sec — locking in your spot'), and set a function timeout of 8–10 s. On a timeout, have the prompt make her say the team will confirm the spot by email rather than read out an error. She must not say it saved (UX-02). Consider enable_backchannel at a low frequency for long answers.

findings.title: Build the Retell path on SDK 3.x now: 2.x and /v2/create-web-call are deprecated on 2026-09-30, and 3.0.1 answers the design doc's open questions
findings.evidence: Deprecation notice: 'Browser JS SDK v2 … Upgrade to SDK 3.x, replace RetellWebClient with RetellClient … Also deprecates POST /v2/create-web-call' on 09/30/2026 (https://docs.retellai.com/deprecation-notice/overview). The 3.0.1 README (2026-09-08) lists onAgentStartTalking/onAgentStopTalking (for the orb), an 'audio' event with emitRawAudioSamples (for the level), mute()/unmute(), end(), startAudioPlayback() to be called from a click (https://docs.retellai.com/deploy/web-call), and optional reCAPTCHA v3 on the public key. retell-migration.md:113-117 still marks these as VERIFY. Its flow (lines 38-42) mints tokens on the server, whereas 3.x RetellClient uses a public key plus a domain allowlist and bypasses src/lib/api-guard.ts.
findings.user_impact: Building on RetellWebClient or startCall would ship on a deprecated path that is removed in 4.0 and force a second migration. Choosing the public-key flow without reCAPTCHA leaves the paid voice minutes open to scripted abuse.
findings.recommendation: Update retell-migration.md to target RetellClient.createWebCall. Drive the orb from onAgentStart/StopTalking plus the audio level (UX-24). Map startAudioPlayback() onto the iPhone 'Play sound' control (composer.tsx:320-338; UX-26). Either enable reCAPTCHA v3 on the public key, or keep server-side creation through /api/retell/web-call behind api-guard, and document which one is used.

findings.title: Retell's audio on iPhone has a recent report of playing through the earpiece, and the page cannot detect it
findings.evidence: livekit/client-sdk-js issue #1836 (opened 2026-03-12, closed): on an iPhone 15 Pro, LiveKit web audio was 'coming from the ear Receiver' while the device list said Speaker (https://github.com/livekit/client-sdk-js/issues/1836). Issue #1568 (iOS 26 Speaker Selection) was closed as not planned (https://github.com/livekit/client-sdk-js/issues/1568). Retell SDK 3.0.1 livekit-transport.ts:43-55,96 passes only deviceId options and calls track.attach(), and its src has no AudioPlaybackStatusChanged handling (scratchpad/ux-audit/mobile/retell-sdk/package/src, grep). bun.lock pins livekit-client 2.22.3. The team fixed exactly this failure for MARY in a5156d2 ('iPhone plays MARY through the speaker, not a phone-call route').
findings.user_impact: If it happens, iPhone visitors hear MARY faintly from the earpiece while holding the phone at arm's length and assume she is broken. That is the symptom PR #1 just fixed.
findings.recommendation: Treat a real-iPhone Retell check as a go-live gate. Add a 'Retell route' test to /soundcheck: join a test call with ?voice=retell, then mark speaker or earpiece, with the ring switch on Ring and on Silent. Keep the Sound chip wired to resumeAudio(), and have it also detach and re-attach the agent track. Don't flip VOICE_PROVIDER until speaker output is confirmed on iPhone 13 (iOS 18) and on iOS 26.

findings.title: With Retell, leaving the app for more than 45 seconds (for example to copy an email) ends the call, where MARY today just waits
findings.evidence: retell/agent.json sets end_call_after_silence_ms 45000. mary-app.tsx:443-447 (5f531ad) hangs up the Retell call on pagehide. LiveKit pauses sending the mic after 5 seconds muted (livekit-client LocalTrack.ts:437-444), and iOS mutes capture in the background (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/689182). On the MARY path, being hidden only flushes the lead (mary-app.tsx:449-458), and the call screen keeps waiting.
findings.user_impact: A visitor who leaves to copy their email from Mail or to answer a message comes back to a call that ended in the middle of signing up.
findings.recommendation: In Retell mode, note the time on visibilitychange→hidden. On return, if the call has ended, show 'Welcome back — pick up where we left off', which runs the existing Resume path (retell.start with the known fields and the same session, so the same sheet row). Consider raising end_call_after_silence_ms to about 90000, or have the agent's first reminder say 'take your time'. Settle this together with the silence limits in UX-29.

findings.title: Real-device checks are still missing for the no-mic path under the silent switch, AirPods mid-call, the Instagram webview and Android
findings.evidence: POSITION.md:122 and PROJECT-STATE.md:67 say Mac Safari, the no-mic path and AirPods are still unproven. /soundcheck already has the no-mic element test (soundcheck.tsx:261, test 4) and the ring-switch selector. The Playwright harness is Chromium with a spoofed Safari user agent, so it cannot reproduce iOS audio sessions, the keyboard or Bluetooth routing. The silent-switch behaviour depends on WebKit putting a MediaStream-backed <audio> in the MediaPlayback category (POSITION.md:80). Web Audio on its own is muted by the switch (https://www.audjust.com/blog/unmute-web-audio-on-ios).
findings.user_impact: 'Type instead' visitors with the silent switch on, and AirPods users, are the most likely next 'she's silent' reports, and nobody has tested them.
findings.recommendation: Run a 15-minute script on the iPhone 13: (1) /soundcheck tests 1-6 with the switch on Silent, then Ring. (2) A 'Type instead' call on Silent. (3) A voice call where AirPods go in after the first answer, two more answers, then the AirPods come out. (4) Low Power Mode on, hands-free, wait 45 s. (5) Open the link from an Instagram DM and from a LinkedIn post. (6) Repeat on Android Chrome and Instagram for Android. Record the results as a table in docs/, and re-run the same matrix with ?voice=retell before switching providers. If the no-mic path is silent on Silent, set navigator.audioSession.type='playback' only when !voiceWanted.

findings.title: Prompt changes reach visitors untested; use Retell's simulation testing, versioning and live monitoring to guard MARY's script
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md says there is no browser or audio test harness, and retell-migration.md:64-68 names grounding discipline as the main risk of porting the prompt. Retell Conductor (2026-07-02) plays scenarios against an agent without dialling, turns failed calls into test cases, and shows proposed changes side by side. Agent Versioning 2.0 (2026-05-27) adds staging and production environment tags plus a Voice Orb share link. Live Call Monitoring (2026-06-19) adds real-time transcripts, scoring by sentiment, latency and interruptions, and listen, whisper or take over (https://www.retellai.com/changelog). SDK 3.x adds monitorCall().takeOver() (README).
findings.user_impact: Prompt changes to MARY currently reach real visitors unverified. Regressions such as re-asking known fields, recording ungrounded details or a mangled email readback are found only by losing leads.
findings.recommendation: For build slice 3, script the five CLOSE scenarios plus the ones in mary-voice.md (early leaver, price objection, 'just email me') and the scenarios in UX-03, UX-11, UX-20, UX-22 and UX-23 as Conductor simulations. Gate every prompt change on staging tags, and share the Voice Orb link for stakeholder review. Give the operator a Live Monitoring view filtered on outcome=callback, so hot leads can be taken over live.

findings.title: Offer 'Call me instead' (a real phone call) for in-app browsers and failed audio, as Retell's own demo does
findings.evidence: Retell's homepage 'Try Our Live Demo' is a form with use case, name and phone, then 'Get a call' (scratchpad/ux-audit/market/sites-ios.json, captured 2026-09-26). Retell's widget has a callback mode with data-tc for a terms URL (https://docs.retellai.com/deploy/chat-widget). MARY's in-app-browser and mic-failure copy can only offer typing (conversation/text.ts:98-118), and the iPhone audio path needs a 'Can't hear her?' escape (composer.tsx:320-338). Outbound AI voice counts as an 'artificial voice' under the TCPA and needs prior express consent (https://justcall.io/blog/ai-voice-agent-disclosure-laws.html, 2026-09-22). Telephony costs from $0.015/min (https://www.retellai.com/pricing).
findings.user_impact: Visitors arriving from Instagram or LinkedIn in-app browsers, people with denied mics, and iPhones with audio trouble currently lose the voice experience entirely. A phone call has none of the browser audio risks.
findings.recommendation: After Retell slice 2, add a secondary 'Rather talk on the phone? We'll call you now' option to the mic-error and in-app-browser notices (UX-07, UX-37). It collects the phone number with an explicit consent checkbox and records the timestamp, then starts an outbound call with the same agent, passing sessionId and the known fields as dynamic variables so MARY continues where the visitor left off.

findings.title: The Apps Script that is deployed is not the one in the repo
findings.evidence: PROJECT-STATE.md:64: 'Hardened Apps Script (rewritten, not Lovable's) deployed ... ping ok (version 2026-09-23)'. The repo copy, docs/google-sheets/Code.gs, is VERSION '2026-09-22' (line 39) with SHARED_SECRET '' (line 27).
findings.user_impact: Whoever next follows docs/google-sheets/README.md redeploys the weaker script, and nobody can review the code that actually receives the leads.
findings.recommendation: Commit the deployed script, without secrets, to docs/google-sheets/Code.gs. Have GET /api/lead compare the ping version against an expected constant.

findings.title: The previous caption ghosts over the new one for about 330 ms on every turn, even with reduced motion
findings.evidence: scratchpad/ux-audit/visual/caption-seq-390.json rows t=725-1062 and t=3245-3562: the exiting line is position:absolute (AnimatePresence mode="popLayout") at opacity 0.95→0 while the new line fades in at the same spot. Screenshots: visual/shots/390x844-light-8-call-after3.png, 1440x900-light-8-call-after3.png, 390x844-light-reduced-8-call-after3.png, and visual/repo/repo-390x844-light-8-call-after3.png (both texts overlap). Code: call-stage.tsx:195 and :222 use popLayout, and the exit {opacity:0, y:-10} is applied even when reduced motion is on.
findings.user_impact: Every reply starts with two sentences printed on top of each other, the most visible unpolished moment on the main screen.
findings.recommendation: For the caption, use mode="wait" with a 120-150 ms opacity-only exit, or crossfade in a grid cell (both children in grid-area:1/1) so they never overlap in space. Drop the y offset when reduced motion is on.

findings.title: Focus falls to <body> at every screen change, the call screen has no heading, and 'You're on the list' is never announced to screen readers
findings.evidence: scratchpad/ux-audit/visual/keyboard.json: afterWelcome, focusAfterClose and endFocus are all '(body)'. The call screen has no headings; only the end screen has an H1. The only live region is inside CallStage (call-stage.tsx:182), so it unmounts when the end screen appears. The document title never changes (endTitle unchanged). The textarea has outline-none and no focus-within style (composer.tsx:284; visual/shots/focus/call2-5.png shows no indicator). Other buttons fall back to the thin browser outline (visual/shots/focus/call2-4.png), unlike the designed ring on Start (visual/shots/focus/landing-0.png).
findings.user_impact: Screen-reader users get no confirmation that the lead was saved, the most important moment of the funnel. After Start they are dropped at the top of an unlabelled page. Keyboard users lose their place on every turn and can't see where the typing focus is.
findings.recommendation: Add an sr-only <h1> 'Talking with MARY' to the call screen. On each stage change, focus the new screen's H1 (tabIndex=-1). Put a persistent polite live region in MaryApp (mary-app.tsx) that announces 'You're on the list, position N' (only when the position is real, UX-02). Set document.title per stage. Add focus-within:shadow-[0_0_0_2px_var(--color-ink)] to the composer shell, and reuse the Start button's focus-visible ring on every button.

findings.title: The 'Conversation so far' panel is not a real modal, and focus is pulled into the composer behind it
findings.evidence: scratchpad/ux-audit/visual/keyboard.json (1440x900, keyboard only): after Enter on 'Show conversation', focus sits on the textarea behind the dialog (dialogOpenFocus), because onSettled calls focusComposer (mary-app.tsx:158-166). aria-modal is null and nothing is inert. Tab goes Close → body → the header buttons behind the overlay. Escape does not close it (dialogAfterEscape: true). After Close, focus goes to <body>, not back to the trigger. axe reports scrollable-region-focusable on the <ol> transcript. Code: call-stage.tsx:34-83. The W3C APG modal dialog pattern requires focus inside on open, Tab trapped, Escape to close, focus returned to the invoker, and aria-modal=true (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/).
findings.user_impact: Keyboard and screen-reader users can't use or leave the transcript panel predictably, and typing aimed at the panel lands in the answer box.
findings.recommendation: Use a real dialog: a native <dialog> with showModal(), or Radix Dialog if it is already a dependency. Suppress focusComposer while the panel is open, make the <ol> focusable (tabIndex=0), and close on Escape and on backdrop click.

findings.title: The screen reader reads MARY's whole line the instant her voice starts, so two voices talk over each other
findings.evidence: call-stage.tsx:181-184 announces `MARY: ${current.text}` through aria-live=polite, and voice-line.ts:96-97 adds the line to the store before speak() starts, so VoiceOver or NVDA speech overlaps MARY's TTS. The status line is aria-live="off" (composer.tsx:312). Notices are role=status elements inserted already filled inside AnimatePresence (composer.tsx:136-146), and MDN warns that live regions added with content may not be announced (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Guides/Live_regions). The orb's role=img label says 'MARY is speaking' on the silent landing (landing.tsx:103).
findings.user_impact: Blind visitors hear MARY and their screen reader say the same sentence at once, and the screen reader's own speech can reach the mic as 'the visitor talking'.
findings.recommendation: When voice is on, announce only the state that matters to the visitor ('MARY is speaking', 'Your turn'), not the text. Offer a 'Read captions aloud' option, or announce the text when voiceOff is true. Keep one always-mounted status region for notices instead of mounting role=status nodes. Mark the landing orb as decorative (aria-hidden).

findings.title: Words MARY has not spoken yet sit at 1.57:1 contrast (axe: serious)
findings.evidence: axe color-contrast violations on the call screen in scratchpad/ux-audit/visual/run-390x844-light.json (call.axe): fg #cbcac7 on #fbfaf7 = 1.57:1 at 20 px, where 4.5:1 is required, and at 26.4 px on desktop, where 3:1 is required. visual/contrast.mjs: ink over the page reaches 3.12:1 at alpha 0.45 and 5.13:1 at 0.6. Code: call-stage.tsx:22 'opacity-20'. The full line is painted ghosted from the moment it is added, before any audio (visual/shots/390x844-light-3-call-speaking-start.png).
findings.user_impact: Low-vision readers, and anyone in sunlight, can't read ahead or read along. During the speech start delay, the whole sentence shows as a faint grey block.
findings.recommendation: Either raise unrevealed words to opacity 0.6 or more on phones (0.45 or more at 24 px and above) and keep the karaoke contrast step small, or don't paint unrevealed words at all and reserve their space with `invisible`, so words appear as she says them.

findings.title: Key call-screen guidance is 9.9 px on phones (live)
findings.evidence: Text survey on live (scratchpad/ux-audit/visual/run-375x667-light.json): 'MARY is speaking · hold to cut in' and 'Hold the button while you talk…' are 9.9 px; 'Can't hear her?…' and 'Play sound' are 9.9 px; progress pills are 10.4 px; end-screen field labels, the landing footer and the 'MARY ·' label are 9.9 px. Repo equivalents: composer.tsx:303 text-[0.7rem] (11.2 px), landing.tsx:34 and end-screen.tsx:163 text-[0.62rem]. Apple HIG lists 11 pt as the minimum iOS text size (https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/typography).
findings.user_impact: The one sentence that explains how to talk to MARY is the smallest text on the screen, often read at arm's length. This hurts first-call success and makes the UI look cramped rather than premium.
findings.recommendation: Set a floor of 12 px for meta text and 14 px for instructions. Make the hold-mode instruction a 14-15 px line directly above the hold button, and cut the stack of three small lines under the composer to one (see UX-77).

findings.title: Recovery and header controls are below comfortable tap size
findings.evidence: Targets on live (scratchpad/ux-audit/visual/run-390x844-light.json): 'Play sound' 70x19 and 'I can hear her' 83x19; talk-mode and voice toggles 32x44; transcript 'Close' 36x36. The repo is worse (visual/repo/run-repo-390x844-light.json): toggles 40x32, Play 76x21, 'Show conversation' 150x28, 'Start another conversation' 150x16. Code: composer.tsx:326/333 py-0.5; call-stage.tsx:158/169 px-3 py-2; call-stage.tsx:58 size-9. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 sets a 24x24 CSS px minimum (https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html), and Apple HIG recommends 44x44 pt (https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility).
findings.user_impact: The 'I can't hear her' buttons, used at the most stressful moment on an iPhone, are the hardest to hit, and the voice and talk-mode toggles sit next to each other at 32 px wide.
findings.recommendation: Give Play sound and I can hear her min-h-11 px-4, as a chip row (UX-26). Give the header toggles size-11 (44x44) with 8 px between them, and give the dialog Close size-11. Keep 'Start another conversation' at min-h-11 as on live.

findings.title: The progress pills read as a six-field form: they overflow off-screen without a cue, show the optional phone as required, use jargon, and give screen readers no done/next state
findings.evidence: On phones the row is cut mid-word ('Real e', 'Bright') with the scrollbar hidden (scratchpad/ux-audit/visual/shots/375x667-light-7-call-long-caption.png, 390x844-light-8-call-after3.png). At 768 px the header pills slide under the 'Quiet room' button ('Busine', visual/shots/768x1024-light-5-call-idle.png). Code: progress-pills.tsx:14 'no-scrollbar … overflow-x-auto'. The pills list all six WAITLIST_FIELDS, including 'Phone', which the playbook marks optional (docs/mary-voice.md §4), and 'Operations' (progress-pills.tsx:17-45; funnel shots/voice-ios-08-mid-welcome.png). State is shown only by a dot or a lime ring; the ring is 1.85:1 against the card (visual/contrast.mjs), and each <li> has no text for done or next. axe reports scrollable-region-focusable on the pill <ul>.
findings.user_impact: Visitors can't see which detail comes next, or that there are six, so the 'two minutes' promise has no visible progress. The row suggests the phone number is mandatory. Screen-reader users hear 'Sarah Okafor, Email, Phone…' with no sense of what is done or pending.
findings.recommendation: On phones, replace the scroller with a compact '3 of 6 · Email next' line plus a 6-dot meter, and keep the full pills from md up. Add an edge fade and scroll the next pill into view (scrollIntoView({inline:'nearest'})). Show Phone as '(optional)', or hide it until asked, and rename 'Operations' to 'How you work'. Add sr-only 'saved' or 'next' text, and use a checkmark icon rather than a colour-only ring. With Retell, the pill data needs the feed described in UX-24.

findings.title: motion/react ignores prefers-reduced-motion: the orb still flies and scales between screens
findings.evidence: scratchpad/ux-audit/visual/motion-probe.mjs with reducedMotion=reduce: 58 distinct orb positions over about 650 ms after Start (216→203 px, y 253→184), the same spring as without reduce. There is no MotionConfig anywhere in src (grep). Motion's docs say the default reducedMotion is "never", and that "user" disables transform and layout animations while keeping opacity (https://motion.dev/docs/react-motion-config). Only some components guard `initial` with useReducedMotion. layoutId is set at call-stage.tsx:188 and on the landing and end screens, and the exit y offsets are not guarded.
findings.user_impact: Visitors who asked their OS for less motion still get the shared-element flight on every screen change and sliding caption exits on every turn.
findings.recommendation: Wrap <LayoutGroup> in mary-app.tsx with <MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">. This removes the layout, transform and y animations globally, keeps the opacity fades, and makes most per-component `reduced ? … :` branches unnecessary.

findings.title: The orb redraws at 60 fps in every state, forever, including on the static end screen
findings.evidence: scratchpad/ux-audit/visual/perf-ios-x1-no-preference.json vs perf-ios-x1-reduce.json (same flow; the orb is static when reduced). End screen idle: 482 vs 242 rAF callbacks in 4 s, so the orb adds 60 frames/s indefinitely. Main thread busy (CDP TaskDuration): landing 97% vs 1.3%, speaking 93.6% vs 3.2%, end 52.6% vs 2.7%. With the CPU throttled 4x (perf-ios-x4-no-preference.json): about 40 fps, p50 33 ms on the landing. The orb's own JavaScript is small (5.9-11.6 ms/s), so the cost is GPU presentation. The runner uses SwiftShader software GL, so the absolute numbers apply to software-GL devices, not to an iPhone 13. Also seen: a 1348 ms long task during load at 4x, and 131-184 ms frames right after Start while the orb flight animates. Code: mary-orb.tsx:134-157 (the loop never idles); orb-renderer.ts:70 antialias:true, although the shader already anti-aliases the edge with smoothstep; mary-orb.tsx:101 DPR cap 1.5 (324x324 canvas at 390 px).
findings.user_impact: Constant GPU work drains phone batteries on a page people leave open after signing up. On software-GL or low-end devices it causes dropped frames exactly during transitions and speech.
findings.recommendation: In mary-orb.tsx, stop the loop in 'done' about 2 s after the bloom settles. Drop to about 24-30 fps in idle and listening, using full rate only while speaking or hearing. Pause the landing orb after about 10 s without interaction. In orb-renderer.ts:70, set antialias:false and powerPreference:'low-power'. Fall back to the 2D or static frame when the renderer string contains 'SwiftShader' or frame p95 exceeds 25 ms. With Retell, drive the level at 30 Hz or less (UX-24).

findings.title: Tablet landing: MARY's preview card is cut off at the right edge from 640 to about 830 px wide
findings.evidence: scratchpad/ux-audit/visual/tablet.mjs: at 768x1024 the card spans x 491→811, 43 px past the viewport; at 700x900 it spans 441→761, 61 px past. Screenshots: visual/shots/768x1024-light-1-landing.png, 700x900-light-1-landing.png. Code: landing.tsx:109 'absolute left-[calc(100%-1.5rem)] … w-80 sm:block'.
findings.user_impact: On an iPad in portrait, the hero's own sentence ('Want first access to…') is clipped, which looks broken on the first screen.
findings.recommendation: Switch to the side-card layout only from lg (1024 px and up), and keep the stacked phone layout (card above the orb) for sm and md. Or use `w-[min(20rem,calc(50vw-6rem))]`.

findings.title: The phone number is never offered when the email arrives before the email-ask step
findings.evidence: allCaptured leaves the phone out (mary-prompt.server.ts:89-91). The email-ask phase (:124-125), the only place the phone is offered, is skipped once the email is in. Live call 3 captured the email in the first answer (scratchpad/ux-audit/conversation/live-3.log), so that visitor would go discovery -> reveal -> lanes -> WRAP with no phone offer. The playbook says the phone is 'always offered' (mary-voice.md:144, :513-516).
findings.user_impact: The sales team gets fewer callable leads. The impact is small, because the phone is optional.
findings.recommendation: Offer the phone once, as the followUp of the turn that confirms the email ('Number's optional — want to add one?'), whatever the phase.

findings.title: A callback request can't finish without a phone number
findings.evidence: endingFor() requires name and phone before a callback can end (src/features/mary/conversation/text.ts:54), but the spec also allows 'emailed instead' under CALLBACK (docs/mary-voice.md:299).
findings.user_impact: A visitor who says 'just email me' and won't give a number keeps getting asked for one and never reaches an end state.
findings.recommendation: Let a callback end with name plus email or phone, and show 'We'll email you' on the end screen.

findings.title: Retry notices stay on screen after the visitor switches to typing
findings.evidence: 'Didn't catch that…' and 'Loud in here? Type your answer below instead.' remain after typed messages and cover the caption area (scratchpad/ux-audit/reliability/s02-error-line-6-typed2-plus15s.png). send() (mary-app.tsx:538-544) does not clear missedHold or suggestTyping, unlike onText (mary-app.tsx:196-199).
findings.user_impact: Old error copy sits on top of the conversation and hides MARY's caption on small phones.
findings.recommendation: Clear missedHold and suggestTyping in send() and at the start of each turn.

findings.title: Three to four 'thinking' signals and a stack of small status lines compete during a turn
findings.evidence: scratchpad/ux-audit/visual/shots/390x844-light-2-call-thinking.png shows all at once: the swirling orb, a '…' caption, the hold button reading 'Thinking… hold to talk', the status line 'Thinking…', and the three-part 'Can't hear her?' row. Code: call-stage.tsx:255, composer.tsx:97, composer.tsx:13, composer.tsx:320-338.
findings.user_impact: The bottom of the screen reads as a wall of small warnings rather than one calm voice interface. Premium voice UIs show one state at a time.
findings.recommendation: Let the orb and one state word in the caption area ('Thinking') carry state. Keep the hold button's label constant ('Hold to talk'); note this conflicts with UX-47's per-state button labels, so choose one. Reserve the single status line under the composer for errors and hints.

findings.title: Header controls are inconsistent and cryptic on phones, and the talk-mode toggle breaks the ARIA toggle pattern
findings.evidence: scratchpad/ux-audit/visual/shots/390x844-light-5-call-idle.png: the talk-mode button is a ringed 32x44 capsule showing only a radio-wave icon, next to a bare speaker icon. call-stage.tsx:158 has ring-1 and :169 does not. The 'Quiet room? Go hands-free' label is hidden below sm (call-stage.tsx:161 'hidden sm:inline'; funnel shots/voice-ios-08-mid-welcome.png). Its aria-label changes with state while aria-pressed is also set (call-stage.tsx:152-157). APG: 'it is critical the label on a toggle does not change when its state changes' (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/button/).
findings.user_impact: On phones nobody can tell that the radio icon means 'go hands-free', so mis-taps switch the talk mode, and the two controls look like they come from different apps. Screen readers announce a changing name plus a pressed state.
findings.recommendation: Use one control style: two 44-px pill buttons with an icon and a short visible label ('Hands-free', 'Sound'), or a segmented 'Hold | Hands-free' switch above the composer. Keep a fixed label ('Hands-free') with aria-pressed, or drop aria-pressed and keep the changing label.

findings.title: End screen: the email breaks mid-word, and at 1440x900 the restart link is below the fold
findings.evidence: 'sarah@brightpathrealty.co|m' at 390 px, 'sarah@brightpathre|alty.com' at 768, and 'brightpathrealt|y.com' at 1440 (scratchpad/ux-audit/visual/shots/390x844-light-10-end.png, 768x1024-light-10-end.png, 1440x900-light-10-end.png). 'sarah@brightpath.co / m' on desktop (funnel shots/convo-desktop-21-end-settled.png). Code: end-screen.tsx:162-167 (two-column dl, break-words). The details card ends below 900 px, so 'Start another conversation' needs a scroll on a 1440x900 laptop.
findings.user_impact: The confirmation, the moment that should feel most finished, shows a broken-looking email.
findings.recommendation: Make the email row col-span-2, like operations. Use `break-all` only as a last resort, or `truncate` with a title. Tighten the vertical rhythm on short desktop heights (orb 0.24*vh, mt-6) so the full summary fits within 900 px.

findings.title: Safe-area insets are ignored: in landscape and home-screen mode the notch and status bar overlap the header and composer
findings.evidence: Only env(safe-area-inset-bottom) is used anywhere (call-stage.tsx:289; the live CSS is the same), yet the viewport meta sets viewport-fit=cover (__root.tsx:83-84), so the page extends under the notch. With emulated insets (scratchpad/ux-audit/visual/safe.mjs, CDP Emulation.setSafeAreaInsetsOverride): in landscape env(left/right)=47 px, but the logo starts at x=32 and the voice toggle ends at x=812 (beyond 797). In home-screen portrait (the manifest declares display:standalone), the top inset is 47 px, but the header buttons sit at y=2-46, under the status bar. The header padding is px-8 (32px) at the 750px landscape width (mobile/shots/landscape-local-after-welcome.png). Code: site-frame.tsx:62 (no env() padding), call-stage.tsx:186. There is a report that fixed content near the iOS 26 floating toolbar is clipped (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/800798).
findings.user_impact: In landscape and home-screen mode, the logo, the controls and the composer edges can sit under the notch, the Dynamic Island, the status bar or the rounded corners.
findings.recommendation: Add pt-[env(safe-area-inset-top)] and pl-[max(1rem,env(safe-area-inset-left))] / pr-[max(1rem,env(safe-area-inset-right))] to SiteHeader and the landing, call and end sections. This is cheapest to do together with the landscape layout in UX-13. Check the bottom composer on an iOS 26 device.

findings.title: Brand words (OmniSuite, Omnikom, MARY) are not given to speech recognition or TTS
findings.evidence: The /api/transcribe prompt is generic, with no vocabulary (src/routes/api/transcribe.ts:26-30). Retell has boosted_keywords to bias the transcriber and pronunciation_dictionary to guide synthesis (https://docs.retellai.com/api-references/create-agent). GPT Transcribe added keyword hints (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog, 2026-07-28).
findings.user_impact: 'Omnikom' heard as 'omni com' or 'Omni calm' leaks into transcripts, the sheet and MARY's replies, and a mispronounced brand name on a sales call undercuts credibility.
findings.recommendation: Add the brand words to the current transcribe prompt now. In Retell, set boosted_keywords ['OmniSuite','Omnikom','MARY'] plus common industry terms from the playbook, and add pronunciation_dictionary entries for OmniSuite and Omnikom.

findings.title: No post-call feedback or sentiment signal; Retell's post-call analysis provides one for free
findings.evidence: ElevenLabs' widget can collect feedback 'After conversation' (https://elevenlabs.io/docs/agents-platform/customization/widget), and Sesame's preview asks for 'feedback at the end of your call' (scratchpad/ux-audit/market/shots/sesame-ios.png). Retell post-call analysis always returns call_summary, user_sentiment and call_successful, plus custom boolean, text, number or selector fields, delivered by call_analyzed (https://docs.retellai.com/features/post-call-analysis-overview). MARY's end screen has no feedback, and lessons come only from /api/reflect (mary-app.tsx:95-119).
findings.user_impact: The team can't tell which conversations felt good or bad, or why people declined. A sentiment and summary column is also what a salesperson wants to see before calling a callback lead.
findings.recommendation: Under Retell, add post_call_analysis_data for outcome (selector: joined, callback, declined, incomplete; already in retell-shared.ts:32), industry, business, callback_requested and objection. Write call_summary and user_sentiment into the sheet row and show them in the owner view, but never let analysis overwrite grounded fields (UX-45). Skip building a rating widget unless summaries turn out not to be enough.

findings.title: Retell voice settings: test Expressive Mode and dynamic speed, but keep the Colloquial Model away from confirmations
findings.evidence: Retell's changelog on 2026-06-19 added Expressive Mode (automatic or manual emotion tags such as [sigh] and [long pause]) and a Colloquial Model that 'rewrites how your agent phrases things in real time' (https://www.retellai.com/changelog). Agent config adds enable_dynamic_voice_speed and voice_speed (https://docs.retellai.com/api-references/create-agent). ElevenLabs voices on Retell cost $0.040/min versus $0.015/min for platform voices (https://www.retellai.com/pricing). MARY's playbook depends on exact readback and confirmation lines (docs/mary-voice.md:179-200, e.g. 'sarah, at brightpath dot com — got it.'). Today's voice is Gemini TTS 'Kore' (src/routes/api/speech.ts:35, 50).
findings.user_impact: The right voice settings would make MARY sound more human than today's pipeline, but a real-time rephrasing layer could alter grounded confirmations and the email readback, the lines that must stay exact.
findings.recommendation: A/B two or three voices, including one ElevenLabs voice (about +$0.025/min), with Expressive Mode and dynamic voice speed on. Keep the Colloquial Model off, or verify in Conductor simulations (UX-60) that it never changes readback and confirmation lines.

findings.title: No dark theme, and the browser theme-color does not match the page background
findings.evidence: scratchpad/ux-audit/visual/shots/390x844-dark-1-landing.png renders the same cream light theme under prefers-color-scheme: dark, because styles.css:79 forces color-scheme: light and the .dark variant is never applied. theme-color is #f8f7f2 (src/routes/__root.tsx:87, public/site.webmanifest), but the page background token computes to #fbfaf7 (visual/contrast.mjs), leaving a faint seam where the browser chrome is tinted. The orb shader's ground shadow is tuned for cream paper (orb-renderer.ts header comment and shadow term).
findings.user_impact: Night-time visitors in dark mode get a bright full-screen page, and the toolbar tint is slightly off.
findings.recommendation: Now: set theme-color and the manifest colours to #fbfaf7 (S). A proper dark call screen (ink background, a lighter shadow term in the shader) is optional polish and not needed for launch.

findings.title: The gap register the docs rely on is not in the repo
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:7 and PROJECT-STATE.md:60 point to docs/audit/GAP-REGISTER.md, and retell-migration.md cites VA-01…VA-10, AI-04 and D2 from it. `git log --all -- docs/audit` returns nothing, and the file exists on no branch. PROJECT-STATE.md:63 says docs/audit is excluded from git.
findings.user_impact: There is no way to check which known gaps are still open, and the Retell plan's 'what this fixes' list can't be verified.
findings.recommendation: Commit docs/audit/ (the register and area files, without secrets), or remove the references. Add the findings in this list to it, with status.
